477.title: Presentation by the Representatives of CLI on Agenda Item No. 3.1 of the 476th RC Meeting. The representative of Crop Life India & Crop Care Federation of India made a joint representation on the subject in reference to the RC decision taken in its 476th meeting vide agenda item no. 3.1 on the issue of changes/modifications in the present guidelines formed in 347th RC meeting and later on revised in 380th RC meeting for Export related. The representatives explained the earlier guidelines and benefits of those guidelines. They requested to allow unregistered molecules for import for export and registered molecules from registered source in general category.
477.decision: After detailed deliberations on the issue decided that unregistered molecules for import for export in general category is allowed to enhance the export opportunities and ease of doing business. However, keeping in view the registered molecule usage in India and its possibilities of pilferage into Indian market, RC reiterated its earlier decision on the registration of registered molecules from registered source with confirm order only. The approved guidelines for unregistered molecules for import for export from any source in general category are attached as Annexure-2.1.1. The validity of the certificate shall be one year from the date of issue of the CR or till the time the molecule is registered for use in the country, whichever is earlier. The RC further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to add these guidelines in the existing guidelines approved by RC in its 380th meeting and make a consolidated guideline. The same shall be put-up on the website for information of the stake holders.

477.title: Gazette Notification No. S.O. 5234 E dared 22.09.2026 issued by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare regarding prohibition of Paraquat Dichloride-Reg.
477.decision: RC perused the above notification issued by the central government wherein the Insecticide Paraquat dichloride is Inter-alia completely prohibited for its manufacture, import, distribution, sale and use in the country being hazardous and involves grave risk to the Public at large. Further the CR issued under section 9 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 shall stand cancelled. RC observed that in compliance with the said notification a public notice dated 06.10.2026 has already been issued by the Sectt. of CIB&RC for information and compliance from the stake holders. RC also notes that Haryana Pesticides Manufacturers’ Association (HPMA) had filed a CWP No. 34272 of 2026 challenging the notification dated 22.09.2026 before the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. RC also perused the order dated 14.10.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court where in the petitioner had undertaken that they will neither sale, purchase or manufacture nor import of paraquat dichloride from today onwards. It also directed the respondents that no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners. RC observed that this order is only qua the petitioner’s member companies. A List of the Same is a part of record. RC decided to comply with the same and inter-alia directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC not to call back the CR from the petitioners.

477.title: Submission of the Report of the Committee constituted in 476th Registration Committee meeting held on 10.09.2026 under Agenda Item No. 11.1, regarding correction of chemical composition in products containing Indoxacarb as one of the active ingredients.
477.decision: The Registration Committee considered the report of the Committee constituted vide Agenda Item No. 3.2 of the 469th Registration Committee meeting held on 10.02.2026 and subsequently reconstituted vide Agenda Item No. 11.1 of the 476th Registration Committee meeting held on 10.09.2026, under the Chairmanship of Dr. Poonam Jasrotia, ADG (PP), ICAR, Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The Committee was constituted to examine the registered formulations containing Indoxacarb, the inclusion of isomer ratio in their chemical composition, and the incorporation of isomer ratio requirements in product specifications to establish the distinctiveness of the technical material used in the manufacture of formulations. The Registration Committee appreciated the efforts made by the committee in collecting and analysing all the related information on the issue. The RC noted the findings of the report regarding the registration status of different technical grades of Indoxacarb and their associated stereo isomer ration in Chemical composition. The report indicated that Indoxacarb Technical 67% minimum, registered for indigenous manufacture, specifies a minimum of 50% active S-isomer and a maximum of 17% inactive R-isomer, whereas Indoxacarb Technical 90% minimum, registered under the import category, specifies a minimum of 90% active S-isomer and a maximum of 1% inactive R-isomer. The Committee further noted that the chemical composition, product specifications and Methods of Analysis of the registered Indoxacarb- based formulations do not uniformly provide for the separate determination of both isomers and their ratio. The Registration Committee also took note of the observations recorded in the report concerning the analysis of a referee sample of Indoxacarb 14.5% + Acetamiprid 7.7% SC, wherein the Central Insecticides Laboratory (CIL) observed an isomer profile containing only the active isomer of Indoxacarb. The report further recorded that the technical material corresponding to Indoxacarb Technical 90% minimum was not registered for domestic use under Section 9(4) of the Insecticides Act, 1968. In this context, the Committee noted the importance of establishing the stereoisomeric profile of Indoxacarb in formulations to facilitate verification of the approved technical source and detection of any possible use of unauthorized, unregistered or export-only technical material in formulations intended for domestic use. The report recommended that the chemical composition of all Indoxacarb- based formulations should clearly specify the total Indoxacarb content, active S-isomer content and inactive R-isomer content. It further recommended that the product specifications and Methods of Analysis should incorporate separate limits for total Indoxacarb, active S-isomer and inactive R-isomer, along with the acceptable S & R isomer ratio, as applicable. The report also proposed corrections to the declared Indoxacarb content and product nomenclature of certain registered formulations, as detailed in the report, wherever required, to account for the respective active and inactive isomer contents. As per available records, total Certificate of Registration holders of the indoxacarb as a sole A.I. or as one of the A.I. in combination is shown as Annexure-3.3.1. After detailed deliberations, the Registration Committee agreed with the recommendations of the Committee as contained in the report. The Registration Committee appreciated and commended the Chairman and all members of the Committee for their comprehensive examination of the registration records, scientific assessment of the isomeric composition of Indoxacarb technical grades and formulations, and formulation of recommendations aimed at strengthening product quality assurance, technical-source traceability and regulatory compliance. The Registration Committee agreed with the recommendations of the report regarding the incorporation of total Indoxacarb content, active S- isomer content, inactive R-isomer content and the acceptable S & R isomer ratio, as applicable, in the chemical composition, product specifications and Methods of Analysis of Indoxacarb-based formulations. The proposed corrections to the chemical composition and product nomenclature of the formulations identified in the report were also noted as part of the Committee's recommendations. The Registration Committee decided that the aforesaid decision shall be applicable prospectively as well as retrospectively. Accordingly, the requirements shall apply to all new applications received for registration of Indoxacarb-based formulations, applications presently under scrutiny at various stages of the registration process, and formulations already registered under section 9(3) & 9(4) of the Insecticides Act, 1968. The concerned applicants and existing registrants shall be required to comply with the prescribed requirements regarding chemical composition, product specifications and Methods of Analysis, including stereoisomer profiling, in accordance with the directions and regulatory procedure prescribed by CIB&RC. The Registration Committee further decided that CIB&RC shall issue a public notice for all concerned applicants and registrants of Indoxacarb-based formulations, communicating the formulation-wise corrected chemical composition and the applicable requirements for product specifications and Methods of Analysis, based on the recommendations accepted by the Registration Committee. Revised and approved Chemical identity of Indoxacarb to be replaced in all the CRs & Chemical Compositions by RC of all the registered formulations registered for use in the country and its revised Product Specifications with Method of Analysis are attached as Annexure 3.3.2. The notice shall clearly specify the requirements applicable to applications under scrutiny and formulations already registered, along with the necessary actions and timelines for compliance, as prescribed by CIB&RC. It was also decided there shall be no change in any other of the adjuvants or its quantity or purity what so ever may be. Only nomenclature of Indoxacarb is changed where Indoxacarb containing 75% S-active isomer and 25% in- active isomer has been approved by the RC in the approved formulation. The corrected formulation-wise chemical compositions shall be applicable to all the Certificate of Registration holders of the above said product. A general Public Notice cum endorsement letter shall be issued on the website for information and adoption by all the stake holders giving the revised Chemical composition of all registered formulation containing as one of the A.I. No separate endorsement shall be required for these purposes. The RC further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC that the revised Chemical Composition (With isomeric ratio) along with Product Specification and Method of analysis shall be distributed to all the RPTLs/SPTLs and CIL for its use in quality control testing of the formulated product.

477.title: Verification of the CR issued to M/s Yashnee Agrochemicals India Private Limited purported for the product Aluminium Phosphide 56% Tablets & Registration no. CIR-17495/2023-APL (442).
477.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that the applicant M/s Yashnee Agrochemicals India Private Limited had submitted a forged and fake CR to the Agricultural Pesticides Registration Authority at ECUADORS for the product Aluminium Phosphide 56% Tablets. RC also observed that the overseas regulatory authority had requested the Secretary CIB&RC for verification of the genuineness of the CR which as per records was not found to be genuine and issued by the RC. Accordingly, the same was communicated to the overseas regulatory authority. RC took a serious note of the same and apparently observed that the act committed by the applicant is unethical, illegal and amount to the commission of grave offence by tempering with the statutory document issued by the RC a regulatory authority under the Insecticides act, 1968. RC also feels it expedient that an opportunity to show cause is required to be given to the applicant to explain their conduct in the matter before taking any adverse view. RC directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a show cause notice to the applicant granting two weeks’ time to submit their reply. Thereafter, the matter may be placed before the RC by the concerned technical expert.
477.company: Yashnee Agrochemicals India Private Limited purported

477.title: Follow up of agenda item no. 10.2 of 476 RC meeting held on 10.09.26 regarding application no. EN-48276 for endorsement of change of address of the source of Mis. Indofil Industries Ltd. under section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act 1968 approved by the RC in its 459th Meeting held on 03.10.2024 at Agenda item No. 9.105.
477.decision: RC perused the fact presented in terms of 476th RC decision and apparently observed that the applicant M/s Indofil Industries Ltd. despite the rejection of their chemistry endorsement application on merits by the RC in its 454th meeting itemized at agenda item no 10.18 had again applied for the same captioned chemistry endorsement vide a fresh application on the very same basis. Since, RC was unaware of the earlier rejection and therefore the same was approved by the RC in its 459th meeting and the certificate to this effect had also been issued by the CIB&RC through CROP Portal. RC after deliberations observes that such act of the applicant is purely unethical, and unwarranted especially in view of the fact that the applicant has neither filed an appeal against the rejection order passed by the RC nor the applicant had represented before the RC to review its decision rejecting the application of the applicant. RC apparently is of the view that once an application is rejected, no fresh application lies, thereafter on identical/similar grounds. RC is of the prima-facie view that such act of M/s Indofil Industries Ltd. and prima-facie tantamount to concealment of facts and is akin to play deception upon the Registration Committee, a statutory body constituted under the Insecticides Act, 1968. However, RC is of the considered view that before taking any coercive action against M/s Indofil Industries Ltd., an opportunity is required to be given to them to explain their stand in the matter explaining their conduct. RC also directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to call the applicant for making a presentation in the next RC meeting so as to take a final decision in the matter. RC also directs the applicant to submit the presentation document well in advance before the secretariat of CIB&RC.

476.title: Presentation by M/s UPL Ltd., regarding for the application of S-Metolachlor Technical u/s 9(3) TIM.
476.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in its 472nd Meeting under Agenda Item No. 10.43, wherein the applicant was directed to make a detailed presentation before the Committee for further consideration. Accordingly, M/s UPL Limited made a presentation before the Committee and submitted, inter alia, that the toxicological profiles and impurity profiles of S-Metolachlor and Metolachlor are comparable and proposed that the available toxicity data on Metolachlor may be considered for the safety assessment of S-Metolachlor based on the bridging rationale. The Committee deliberated upon the submissions made by the applicant. After due consideration, the Committee directed the applicant to submit the requisite toxicity data in accordance with the prescribed guideline applicable to registration under Section 9(3) TIM. The matter may accordingly be considered further upon submission and evaluation of the requisite toxicity data in accordance with the applicable requirements.

476.title: Representation received from stakeholders for revisiting the Registration requirement and the modalities for grant of registrations under "Export Only" and "Import for Export" categories.
476.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in details and observed that the requested guidelines use to be in existence and formulated in 347th RC which was later on revised in 380th RC meeting. The RC was of the opinion that the spillage/leaching of unregistered molecules may infiltrate into Indian market, so before deciding on the guidelines it was felt appropriate that Crop Life India may be asked for a detailed presentation regarding the changes proposed along with the present provisions under which the export certificates for Import for Export on unregistered molecules category are received from unregistered source and suggest SOP/procedure/conditions to contain/regulate while avoiding Indian market access/use. RC also directed them to present details about the issues encountered wrt to the present guidelines for Export u/s 9(3).

476.title: Confirmation of Data Verification/Generation by concerned institutes/labs submitted along with the application for registration of insecticide. In continuation to the decision taken in its 468th meeting vide agenda item no. 3.1, RC again reiterated that the need for verification of data/reports pertaining to various toxicity or other studies generated in NABL/GLP conditions may be taken on case-to-case basis for ascertaining the authenticity of the studies comprehensively by the Sectt. of CIB&RC. 476.decision: RC decided that a team of one expert from Sectt. of CIB&RC and one officers nominated by the NGCMA in case of GLP and a team of two officers from the Sectt. of CIB&RC in case of NABL may be deputed as and when needs arise on-site evaluation of study-specific data/reports.

476.title: Consideration of an application of M/s PI Industries Ltd. for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Pioxaniliprole Technical 97.5% w/w min. under section 9(3) TIM of the Insecticide Act, 1968.
476.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and considered the application of Pioxaniliprole Technical (97.5% w/w min.) U/S 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968 in TIM category. The RC was informed that the applicant has claimed that this molecule is invented and ready for launch in India even before registration in any other country of the world. This molecule has been scrutinized as per the definition of New Molecule decided in 434th Meeting held on 30.11.2021 and under "Make in India" initiatives approved by the RC in its 437th Meeting held on 16.03.2022. The Committee observed that Pioxaniliprole is the first insecticide active ingredient discovered in India; applied for registration under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides under TIM and FIM category. The Committee noted that the present application gives practical effect to its aforesaid decisions on indigenous capability in crop protection chemicals and is in consonance with the objective of the Government of India of promoting research and development within the country and the development of indigenous technologies for the benefit of the Indian farmer. The RC decided to approve for grant of registration for Technical Indigenous manufacture of Pioxaniliprole Technical 97.5% w/w min. under section 9(3), with a provisional shelf life of two years. The following condition may also be incorporated in the CR or L/L wherever applicable: “The applicant is required to submit real time / actual storage stability study data in the proposed construct and container of sale for duration of minimum 30 months, within two and half years of submission of application for granting the registration, failing which Registration Certificate shall be deemed cancelled.”

476.title: Consideration of application of M/s Saraswati Agrochemcials India Pvt. Ltd., for grant of registration of Formetanate hydrochloride Technical 92% w/w Min. for import under section 9(3) TI of the Insecticide Act, 1968.
476.decision: RC discussed and deliberated the agenda in details and observed that various issues pertaining to the application needs to be addressed properly. Therefore, the RC feels expedient to call the applicant to make a presentation in the next RC meeting on the following points of concern on Formetanate hydrochloride: 1. Formetanate hydrochloride belong to WHO classification by hazard category 1b i.e. highly hazardous pesticide. Since the molecule belong to bright red colour toxicity triangle pesticide, absolute necessity may be justified. 2. The nitrosamine impurity N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) which seems to be a probable carcinogen, which may arise from the presence of the N-dimethylamino group, has not been disclosed in the chemical composition. Furthermore, this impurity may also form during storage and also in field. 3. The toxicology studies submitted by the applicant have been sponsored by various companies and none of these studies was sponsored by the proposed manufacturer i.e. Sunko Ink co Ltd, Taiwan. Therefore, the applicant is required to establish the linkage between the respective study sponsors and the proposed manufacturer through authorization. 4. Purity of technical material used to conduct acute inhalation toxicity study, skin sensitization study, repeated dose dermal toxicity study is below the proposed minimum purity of 92%. 5. Chemical composition of the technical material used in teratology study of rat, unscheduled DNA Repair in cultured mammalian cells and mouse lymphoma assay is different from the proposed chemical composition in Form 1. 6. Waiver request for repeated dose inhalation toxicity study need justification keeping in view the following: a) Formetanate hydrochloride is highly toxic by the inhalation route, with an acute inhalation LC50 of 0.15 mg/l. b) Lungs are the highly vascular organ due massive surface area and thin epithelial lining. Therefore, chemical absorbed through this route can rapidly enter the systemic circulation, potentially resulting in systemic toxicity. c) Formetanate hydrochloride is highly water soluble and dissolve readily in respiratory tract lining fluids and alveolar surfactant. Hence, absorbs rapidly. d) Repeated inhalation exposure may cause persistent and cumulative pulmonary effects like inflammation, tissue injury or fibrosis. 7. Waiver request for developmental and delayed neurotoxicity study need justification considering it is a mandatory requirement for pesticides classified as neurotoxicants, particularly in view of the pesticide’s proposed mode of action and recurrent findings of neurotoxicity observed in sub-chronic and chronic studies. 8. Formetanate hydrochloride is a water soluble N-methylcarbamate insecticide that may pose high potential risk for leaching into soil and contaminate groundwater. Potential risk of Ground water contamination keeping in view its proposed label claims on onion and chilli and major metabolites of plant/soil/water. 9. Global status of the molecule regarding its restriction, withdrawn, banned. After detailed deliberations, it was decided to call the applicant for presentation on the issues.

476.title: Follow up of agenda item no. 10.13 of 470 RC meeting pertaining to the compliance of order dated 06.02.2026 passed by the Appellate Authority in revision petition no. 03 of 2025 M/s. Shobikaa v/s CIB&RC in FIM vs FI Deltamethrin LLIN matter.
476.decision: RC perused the agenda and at the outset observed that the above matter is being dealt on the directions of the Appellate Authority passed in Revision Petition No 03 of 2025 vide Order dated 06.02.2026 mentioning that the gamut of technical aspects involved in the matter are also required to be re-examined by the RC and in case of requirement, a consultative process may be adopted with ICMR, the apex body for framing the protocols w.r.t evaluation of public health Insecticides having adequate technical competence. In such situation, the petitioner shall also be at liberty to present their point of view. Subsequently, the matter was placed in the 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 (Vide agenda item no. 10.13). The decided as under: "RC deliberated the agenda in detail and directed the Secretary, CIB&RC to discuss the issues with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) strictly as per the observations of Hon’ble Appellate Authority in its order dated 06.02.2026 at the level of Secretariat of CIB&RC. The copy of the order is also to be shared with ICMR. The concerned bio efficacy expert is directed to submit the detailed report to the Registration Committee for further deliberations". In order to comply with the order passed by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority on 06th February 2026 and the decision of 470th RC meeting, the Secretary, Central Insecticide Board and Registration Committee (CIB&RC) convened a meeting with the Scientists of ICMR & NIMR in the Secretariat of CIB&RC, Faridabad. During the meeting, the Scientists from ICMR and NIMR informed that the matter needs to be discussed in the ICMR- Expert group on Evaluation of Vector Control Products (EVCP). RC also observes that since the comments from the ICMR were awaited and therefore the RC could not take a final decision in the matter within the stipulated timelines. The bio-efficacy expert informed that the ICMR had now submitted their inputs in the matter in terms of consultative process adopted by the RC with ICMR. RC also perused the letter dated 08.09.2026 issued by Dr. Nivedita Gupta, Scientist- G, ICMR addressed to Secretary, CIB&RC. In terms of the observations made by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority, the aforesaid inputs provided by the ICMR must also be shared with M/s Shobikaa Impex Pvt. Ltd., the petitioner in the matter to also present their response thereto. RC accordingly decided and directs the concerned bio-efficacy expert to share the complete communication dated 08.09.2026 received from the ICMR to M/s Shobikaa Impex Pvt Ltd. Further the Secretariate of CIB&RC is directed to invite M/s Shobikaa Impex Pvt. Ltd. in the next RC meeting to make a presentation in this regard so as to enable the RC to take a final view in the matter in terms of the observations and directions made by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority in its order dated 06.02.2026.

476.title: Minutes of Meeting chaired by AS(PP) on 19.08.2026 to review the matters pertaining to CIB&RC (Dte. of PPQ&S)-reg
476.decision: The RC deliberated the MOM and decided as under: 1. No application of registration U/S 9(3) TIM/FIM/TI/FI/TI (New Source) shall be allotted, henceforth to legal section in case of KYC of that applicant is already done. 2. No application of registration U/S 9(4) TIM shall be allotted, henceforth to legal section in case of KYC of that applicant is already done. 3. Team CGG may be asked to revamp the CROP portal keeping in view of technological upgradation and requirement of regulatory authority for review and to make it user friendly. 4. Dual authentication for login by all users including the applicants as well as Experts shall be made mandatory. 5. The accounts of the Experts shall be devised on the basis of their designation and work handled. 6. The RC directed the Secretary (CIB&RC) to periodically review the throughput of experts regularly for optimal utilization of available Experts. 7. All Experts are directed to ensure that all the applications shall be disposed-off strictly on a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) basis to ensure a fair, transparent and unbiased disposal. Experts shall be held solely responsible for adhering to the FIFO. 8. The sample drawl process shall be completed in compliance as per the guideline and SOP approved by RC for drawl of sample. 9. The RC decided pending cases may be taken up on priority by issuing a public/newspaper notice as a final opportunity to all stake holders. In case of continued non-compliance, appropriate cancellation orders shall be passed in accordance with the applicable legal provisions. 10. The RC further directed the Under Secretary (CIB&RC) to submit the detailed factual position on e-KYC containing such as: a. E-KYC compliant users b. Details of accounts which has been merged into which account c. Details of the applicants for which notices have been received back being undelivered. d. Details of accounts which has not applied for merger/revival etc with name details of Certificate of Registration issued to those accounts. e. Details of the accounts, Officer address, Manufacturing address and CR issued into those accounts which shall be published in the newspaper for wide information. f. Details of communications sent to the State Govt for communicating the notice of non-compliance of e-KYC to the companies. g. Other details which may be necessary. h. RC further directed to the Secretary, CIB&RC to communicate this decision to the stakeholders for compliance.

476.title: Reducing the pendency of bio-pesticides applications and analysis of 16Sr DNA finger printing from NBAIM. A meeting was held on 16th September 2026 among officials of Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIB&RC) and ICAR-National Bureau of Agriculturally Important Microorganisms (ICAR-NBAIM), Mau, under the chairmanship of Dr. Poonam Jasrotia, ADG (PP&B) to deliberate upon issues related to the generation, processing and submission of DNA finger printing reports of biopesticides through the CROP portal. The MOM of the above meeting has been circulated to all the RC, members presented in the meeting through email for discussion and decision. The MOM is attached as Annexure- 11.2.1. After discussion and deliberation telephonically on the issue it was decided that all the biopesticides applicants needs to submit a sample in NBAIM for 16 Sr DNA Printing and sample receipt of the same is to be uploaded into the CROP portal as a proof as per existing guidelines. It is observed that many applicants are submitting sample in NBAIM but not submitting the application in CROP portal. Therefore, it is decided to redefine the flow for filling of application of bio- pesticides as under: 1. The applicant has to submit the application of the biopesticides into the CROP portal after paying requisite fees. 2. The applicant has to submit 500 gm sample of biopesticide as per guidelines of registration in ICAR-National Bureau of Agriculturally Important Microorganisms (NBAIM), Kushmaur, Mau Nath Bhanjan 275103 (U.P.) India mentioning the application number generated in CROP portal; within 30 days from the submission of application in CROP portal. 3. The applicant has to submit 500 gm sample of biopesticide as per guidelines of registration in Central Insecticides Laboratory mentioning the application number generated in CROP portal; within 30 days from the submission of application in CROP portal. 4. A Notification for submission of receipt of samples in CIL & NBAIM will be reflected in the concerned login in CROP immediately after submission of application. 5. The applicant has to submit the sample submission receipt of CIL & NBAIM clicking on the notification shown in CROP in the respective login ID of applicants. 6. A track option for CIL and NBAIM to verify the status of submission of application at the time of submission of sample shall be created by CGG. 7. The application automatically shall be deemed rejected, in case of non- submission of receipt in prescribed time line (30) days. 8. The concerned expert has to prepare a list of such cases and putup to RC for approval of rejection.
476.decision: The RC directed the Secretary (CIB&RC) to issue a public notice for the awareness of all the stake holders and team CGG to redefined the flow of filling of application. Meeting ended with a vote of thanks to the Chair *****

475.title: Consideration and compliance of order dated 10.08.2026 passed by the Hon'ble Revisional Authority in Revision Petition No. 02 of 2026 filed by M/s Godrej Agrovet Ltd. Vs. CIB&RC and M/s Best Crop Science Pvt. Ltd.
475.decision: RC perused the Order dated 10.08.2026 passed by the Hon'ble Revisional Authority wherein the matter has been remanded by the Hon'ble Revisional Authority for a limited review of the issues relating to the manufacturing process, impurity profile, chemical equivalence and the consequential safety implications arising therefrom. RC also perused the letter dated 13.08.2026 from M/s Godrej Agrovet ltd. The Committee was apprised that, in compliance with the directions of the Hon'ble Revisional Authority, the complete chemistry dossier and all documents available on record were re-examined. The Committee noted that the applicant had submitted the requisite documents prescribed under the extant TIM vs. TI Guidelines, including the list of raw materials and intermediates with source of supply, stepwise manufacturing process, chemical equations, flow sheet diagram from raw materials to the final technical product, effluent treatment method, specifications, method of analysis, impurity profile and supporting analytical data. The Committee further noted that chemical equivalence had already been established with the registered source, M/s Godrej Agrovet Limited, and that the chemical composition, specifications and impurity limits submitted by the applicant were identical to those of the registered source. The Committee also noted that an in-process sample drawn during inspection by officers of the Directorate had been tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory (CIL) and found to conform to the submitted specifications. The CIL analysis did not reveal any unidentified impurity or any additional impurity having any toxicological concern. The reported impurity profile was within the prescribed limits and no toxicologically significant impurity arising from the disclosed manufacturing process was detected. The Committee further deliberated upon the concerns raised before the Hon'ble Revisional Authority regarding the manufacturing process and the possible formation of toxicologically significant impurities. After examining the chemistry dossier, impurity profile, CIL analytical report and other material available on record, the Committee observed that no chemistry- related deficiency or safety concern has been established. The available data do not indicate the formation or presence of any additional toxicologically significant impurity under the disclosed manufacturing process. The RC also noted that the petitioner's contention regarding the use of chloroform during the manufacturing process, including the alleged possibility of the formation of Methoxy Isocyanide and it’s derivatives or any other additional impurities arising therefrom, is not revealed from the technical dossier or the reports available on record. The Committee observed that no such concerns are reflected in the technical documentation or analytical reports submitted by the applicant or generated by the Central Insecticides Laboratory. Accordingly, the RC found no merit or substance in the averments made by the petitioner in this regard. Accordingly, the Registration Committee, after thorough re-examination of the matter in compliance with the Order dated 10.08.2026 of the Hon'ble Revisional Authority and considering the available material on records, found no reason to interfere with its earlier decision taken in the 471st RC Meeting under Agenda Item No. 6.59, to grant registration for the indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5% Min. under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968, in the TIM vs. TI category, to M/s Best Crop Science Pvt. Ltd. The Committee, therefore, decided to uphold its earlier decision for grant of registration for Technical Indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.50 % w/w Min. under section 9(3) TIM vs TI, with a provisional shelf life of two years. The applicant has to submit the real time shelf-life data as per existing guideline of RC within two and half years of submission of application for granting the registration, failing which Registration Certificate shall be deemed cancelled. A condition shall be incorporated in the CR of the applicant. It was further decided that the formulation files containing Fluxametamide in solo or combination pending as on date shall be put up to RC in next meeting of RC. RC directs the Secretary, CIB&RC to communicate this decision to the Hon’ble Revisional Authority and the respective parties.

475.title: Consideration of the representation of M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd. regarding the requirement of mutagenicity data for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Bensulfuron Methyl Technical 97% w/w min. under Section 9(3) TIM (TIM vs. TI) of the Insecticides Act, 1968.
475.decision: The Committee considered the representation of M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd. seeking waiver of the mutagenicity data requirement, with reference to the decision of the 473rd RC Meeting vide Agenda Item No. 6.7. The applicant submitted that the studies were initiated on 23.12.2019 and completed on 22.06.2022 under the data requirements prevailing at that time and claimed that mutagenicity data were not required where chemical equivalence with the earlier Section 9(3) registered technical was established. The applicant further submitted that the data requirements were subsequently revised pursuant to the 442nd RC Meeting held on 18.11.2022, i.e. after completion of the studies. The applicant also relied upon the decision of the 424th RC Meeting vide Agenda Item No. 10.26, contending that the RC had considered mutagenicity data as not required where chemical equivalence had been established. The Committee, after deliberation, observed that the present application was submitted on 21.02.2023, subsequent to the 442nd RC Meeting dated 18.11.2022, wherein the applicable toxicological data requirements included submission of mutagenicity data. The Committee further observed that the decision of the 424th RC Meeting pertained to Section 9(4) TIM applications and were not applicable to the present Section 9(3) TIM application. Further, evidence establishing chemical equivalence with the earlier Section 9(3) registered technical has not been furnished. The Committee, after deliberation, observed that, as per the “Guidance Document on Toxicology for Registration of Chemical Pesticides”, adopted in the 377th RC meeting, read with the relevant data requirements approved in the 381st, 440th, 442nd and 449th RC meetings, the prescribed mutagenicity data are mandatory requirement for toxicological evaluation and characterization of the genotoxic potential of the technical grade active ingredient. In the absence of such data, the genotoxic hazard profile cannot be adequately characterized for a scientifically sound safety assessment. Accordingly, the Committee did not find sufficient justification for waiver of the prescribed mutagenicity data and decided that the applicant shall submit the complete mutagenicity data package as per the applicable guidelines for further scientific evaluation and consideration of the application.

474.title: Presentation by M/s Ecoplants Co. Limited, with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.50 of the 472nd Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding technical presentation on 1-Methylcyclopropene(1-MCP) 12% Gas Generating.
474.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 472nd RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 10.50), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation regarding the proposed registration of 1-Methylcyclopropene (1-MCP) 12% Gas Generating (GE) formulation. The representative of M/s Ecoplants Co. Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that the proposed product is a gas-generating formulation wherein the active ingredient, 1-Methylcyclopropene (1-MCP), is not manufactured, isolated or supplied as a conventional technical grade material. Instead, 1-MCP gas is generated in situ immediately prior to application by mixing two imported precursor components in a dedicated gas generator under controlled heating conditions, and the generated gas is directly released into sealed post-harvest chambers for use through a specially designed gas generator. The applicant submitted that, owing to this mode of generation, no standalone technical grade active ingredient exists in the conventional sense. It was further submitted that the product is intended exclusively for indoor post- harvest application in sealed chambers by trained personnel only, without direct exposure to soil, water or non-target organisms. Accordingly, the applicant requested the Registration Committee to frame an appropriate regulatory framework for registration of 1-MCP gas-generating systems and sought waiver of the technical and ecotoxicity data requirements on the ground that such data are not scientifically applicable to the proposed product. It was also informed that their product is already registered in various countries globally. After detailed deliberation, the Committee appreciated the utility of the proposed technology and accordingly, decided to constitute an expert group to examine the scientific and regulatory aspects of the proposal to recommend an appropriate regulatory framework for consideration. Further, the composition of the expert group as under: 1. Dr. K.L. Gurjar, JD (PP)-Chairman 2. Dr. Sonai Rajan, AD (Entomology)-Member 3. Dr. Swati Som, AD (Toxicology)-Member 4. Ms. Vineta Maheshwari, PPO (Chemistry)-Member Secretary

474.title: Presentation by M/s Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.43 of the 470th Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding for the registration of s-Metolachlor technical 96 % Min. u/s 9(3) TI.
474.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 470th RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 10.43), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation to justify the adequacy of the submitted toxicological data in view of the use of test material with variable purity, the non-submission of a combined chronic toxicity/carcinogenicity study in rats, and the tumor findings observed in the submitted two-year rat oncogenicity study for the registration of s-Metolachlor technical 96 % Min. u/s 9(3) TI. The representative of M/s Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that S-Metolachlor is an enriched isomer of Metolachlor, requiring approximately 40% lower application rates than Metolachlor, thereby reducing operator exposure and environmental loading. The applicant submitted that a complete toxicological data package specific to S-Metolachlor has been generated and submitted in support of the application. It was further submitted that the bridging approach has been proposed only with respect to the chronic toxicity/carcinogenicity endpoint, based on the comparable metabolic profile and toxicological behavior of S-Metolachlor and Metolachlor. The applicant further stated that such scientific bridging has been accepted by regulatory authorities in several jurisdictions, including the USA, Canada, Brazil, Australia, Japan and the European Union, and referred to previous RC decisions wherein isomer-specific bridging was considered based on the overall weight of scientific evidence. The applicant further submitted that 12 of the 14 batches used in the toxicological studies met the minimum purity specification of 96%, while the remaining two batches had purity between 95% and 96%, with no batch below 95%. It was contended that the observed variation falls within the acceptable limits prescribed under the FAO specifications. The applicant also presented the proposed constitutive androstane receptor (CAR)-mediated mode of action for liver tumor formation in rats and submitted that the observed hepatocellular tumors are rodent-specific and not relevant to humans. After detailed deliberation, the Committee accepted the applicant's scientific justification regarding the purity variation of the test material used in the toxicological studies. The Committee noted that S-Metolachlor continues to be registered in several major jurisdictions, including the USA, Canada, Japan and Brazil. However, it also noted that the approval of S-Metolachlor was not renewed in the European Union from 2024 due to concerns, inter alia, relating to groundwater contamination and unresolved issues of mutagenicity and carcinogenicity. Accordingly, the Committee directed the applicant to submit adequate scientific evidence addressing the human relevance of the proposed CAR- mediated mode of action, the carcinogenicity concerns, and measures to mitigate groundwater contamination. The Committee further clarified that bridging of toxicological data for isomeric active ingredients shall be considered only on a case-to-case basis based on the totality of scientific evidence and a weight-of-evidence approach, and shall not constitute a general precedent. The matter shall be considered further upon submission and evaluation of the requisite information by the applicant.

474.title: Presentation by M/s Deccan Fine Chemicals (India) Pvt. Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.27 of the 473rd Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding for representation of application of Florpyrauxifen Benzyl technical 94.0 % w/w Min. u/s 9(3) TIM vs TI.
474.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 473rd RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 10.27), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation regarding the proposal for registration of Florpyrauxifen-benzyl Technical 94.0% w/w Min. under Section 9(3) TIM vs TI, of the Insecticides Act, 1968 wherein the equivalence has been claimed with M/s Corteva Crop India Pvt. Ltd. u/s 9(3) TI with a minimum purity of 92.0% w/w. The representative of M/s Deccan Fine Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that the proposed indigenous technical has been developed through technology transfer from M/s Corteva Agriscience LLC under the Make in India initiative, with an improved manufacturing process resulting in an increase in the minimum purity from 92.0% w/w to 94.0% w/w. They further stated that this site shall be supplying this product to M/s Corteva Agriscience LLC for global supply. The technology of manufacturing Florpyrauxifen – benzyl (Rinskor™) technical is developed by M/s. Corteva Crop India Pvt Ltd. The same technology has been transferred to M/s. Deccan Fine Chem Pvt. Ltd. For global supply including India too. The application is complete from Bio-efficacy and Legal divisions, and currently under scrutiny from Toxicology, Chemistry and Packaging divisions. Deccan has submitted replies to Chemistry and Toxicology divisions which are under scrutiny. The current application was discussed in the 473rd meeting of the Registration Committee (RC), vide agenda item 10.27, held on 29.06.2026. The RC decided to call the applicant for presentation. The representatives of the applicant submitted that 94% purity technical manufactured through new route is registered in 68 countries and M/s. Deccan obtained registration for export of 94% pure Rinskor™ technical which is used globally, other than India. They further explained that The US EPA uses the “Test guidelines for pesticides and toxic substances*” Code Federal Regulations 40CFR158 to assess that the active ingredient doesn’t introduce new toxicological or environmental risks. The EU equivalency process follows the “Plant Protection Products Regulation 1107/2009” and uses a two-tiered approach (SANCO-10597/2003): 1. Tier I: Focuses on chemical profiles (identity, analytical profiles of 5- batch analysis, and impurity profiles). 2. Tier II: If Tier I cannot establish equivalency, Tier II requires mammalian toxicity and ecotoxicity testing to determine whether any new impurities increase the overall hazard to health or the environment. 3. Both approaches have been used to demonstrate the equivalency of Florpyrauxifen benzyl from the Deccan source to the US source. The Deccan source has been approved in both the US and EU. Both approaches are compliant with the equivalence assessment method outlined in the “Manual on development and use of FAO and WHO specifications for Pesticides” (2025) The applicant presented the outcome of the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier 1", wherein it was submitted that the Tier 1 criteria, namely: a) The certified minimum purity is not lower than that of the reference source; b) No new impurities are present; c) The limits of relevant impurities, as certified for the reference source, are not increased; and d) The certified limits of all non-relevant impurities are not increased beyond the acceptable limits. The applicant further presented the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier 1 Toxicological Results" and explained that the increase in the certified minimum purity from 92% to 94% w/w and the observed increase in the impurity were evaluated and found acceptable. The applicant further presented the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier 2" and the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier-II Toxicological Results". It was submitted that the proposed source was evaluated through the recommended Tier 2 toxicological studies, including the acute toxicity six-pack and genotoxicity studies, and that the results demonstrated that the Florpyrauxifen-benzyl Technical manufactured by the applicant is toxicologically equivalent to the reference source. The applicant also presented the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Overall Toxicological Results", wherein all relevant impurities were evaluated and concluded to be acceptable under the Tier II FAO equivalence assessment, with no toxicologically relevant impurities identified and no increase in hazard observed. The applicant presented that the registered TI of the same product contains 12 numbers of impurities. The applicant has removed nine number of impurities (including others impurities containing unidentified impurities <0.1 wt%) and two numbers of impurities have been reduced in quantification. Eight number of new impurities have been added/generated in the CC of the present applicant. The applicant further submitted that as per the requirement of 449th meeting, if chemical equivalence is not established, they have submitted additional data to fulfill the regulatory and safety requirement. The Committee observed that the applicant has addressed the requirements of the guidelines approved by the Registration Committee in its 449th meeting regarding assessment of chemical equivalence. The applicant submitted that although an increase in impurity levels was observed due to the improved manufacturing process, in accordance with the provisions of the 449th RC guidelines, which states that: “If impurities are identified, quantified and are not within limits of registered technical or if impurities are not within ±3%) and/or any additional impurity is present then in addition to the tests as indicated in (4) above, additional tests based on the nature and quantity of impurity and QSAR alert will be taken on case-to-case basis.” Therefore, the RC feels that the proposal is in compliance with the 449th RC guidelines on chemical equivalence assessment. The Committee further acknowledged that the implementation of solvent recycling systems in the proposed manufacturing process, leading to a lowered Process Mass Intensity (PMI), decreased raw solvent consumption, reduced metal catalyst dependencies, minimized waste generation, and significant net savings in global warming potential and carbon intensity. The Committee also noted the supporting data submitted for the new Florpyrauxifen-benzyl source specification in key geographies, including the USA, European Union, Australia and Japan, and the applicant's submission that the new source has been accepted by the respective regulatory authorities. After detailed deliberation, the Registration Committee found the chemistry- related justification, chemical equivalence assessment under Tier 1 and Tier 2, toxicological evaluation, manufacturing process improvements and supporting data to be satisfactory and agreed with the proposal for Florpyrauxifen-benzyl Technical 94.0% w/w Min. under Section 9(3) TIM vs TI. The application shall be put up to RC as and when complete in compliance of above decision.

474.title: Presentation by M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 6.55 of the 471st RC Meeting regarding registration of indigenous manufacture of Carfentrazone ethyl Technical 90% w/w Min. under section 9(3) TIM vs TI.
474.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 473rd RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 6.55), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation to justify the non-submission of mutagenicity data required for registration of Carfentrazone- ethyl Technical 90% w/w Min. under Section 9(3) TIM vs TI. The representative of M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that the application was filed on 06.03.2023, and that, as per the then applicable guideline mutagenicity data were not required where the chemical composition is identical to that of the registered Section 9(3) technical. The applicant further submitted that chemical equivalence with the registered Section 9(3) technical had been established and, accordingly, mutagenicity data were not generated. In support of its submission, the applicant referred to the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.26) and submitted that the said decision specifically addressed mutagenicity requirements in relation to chemical equivalence. The applicant also referred to the decisions of the 442nd and 443rd RC Meetings, submitting that the implementation date of the revised Toxicology Guidelines had not been finalized and, therefore, the application should be considered under the applicable guidelines in force at the time of submission. After detailed deliberation, the Committee observed that the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.26) relied upon by the applicant pertained specifically to applications under Section 9(4) TIM and was not applicable to applications under Section 9(3). The Committee was of the view that submission of mutagenicity data is essential for the scientific evaluation of the technical grade active ingredient and for ensuring its safety. Accordingly, the Committee directed the applicant to submit the complete mutagenicity data package in accordance with the applicable Toxicology Guidance Document, including the Ames test and the requisite in vitro and in vivo genotoxicity studies, for further consideration of the application. After detailed deliberation, the Committee observed that the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.26) relied upon by the applicant pertained specifically to applications under Section 9(4) TIM and was not applicable to the present application under Section 9(3). The Committee further observed that the regulatory framework governing the present application, including the Guidance Document on Toxicology for Registration of Chemical Pesticides adopted by the RC in its 376th Meeting and finalized in its 377th Meeting, read together with the guidelines approved by the RC in its 381st, 440th, 442nd and 449th Meetings, requires submission of the mutagenicity data package as an essential component of the toxicological data requirements for the scientific evaluation and safety assessment of technical grade active ingredients. The Committee noted that such data are fundamental for the assessment of the genotoxic potential of the technical grade active ingredient and are indispensable for arriving at a scientifically sound and regulatory-compliant decision regarding its safety. Accordingly, the Committee decided that the applicant shall submit the complete mutagenicity data package as prescribed under the Guidance Document on Toxicology for Registration of Chemical Pesticides, for further scientific evaluation and consideration of the application.

474.title: Presentation by M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 6.62 of the 471st RC Meeting regarding registration of Picoxystrobin 10% + Copper Oxy Chloride 35% WG u/s 9(3) FIM.
474.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 471st RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 6.62), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation to justify higher acute oral toxicity of the formulation than that of the individual technical active ingredients for grant of registration U/s 9(3) FIM. The representative of M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that although the proposed formulation exhibited higher acute oral toxicity (LD₅₀ >300 to ≤2000 mg/kg body weight; GHS Category 4) than the individual technical active ingredients, it falls under the Blue Toxicity Triangle category and does not represent the highly hazardous toxicity classes. The applicant further submitted that the acute dermal toxicity (LD₅₀ >2000 mg/kg body weight) was comparable to both technical active ingredients, while the acute inhalation toxicity (LC₅₀ >4.32 mg/L) was lower than that of Picoxystrobin Technical (>2.12 mg/L) and Copper Oxychloride Technical (2.83 mg/L). The applicant also submitted that the formulation was non-irritant to skin and eyes, whereas the individual technical active ingredients were reported as slight irritants to irritants, and was non-sensitizing, similar to both technical active ingredients. Accordingly, the applicant submitted that the observed increase in acute oral toxicity did not alter the overall hazard classification of the formulation. After detailed deliberation, the Committee found the applicant's scientific justification regarding the higher acute oral toxicity of the proposed formulation to be satisfactory and agreed that the application may be processed further in accordance with the applicable regulatory provisions.

474.title: Consideration of the Report of the Expert Committee on the restricted Use of Glyphosate. At the outset, RC observes that DA&FW is reviewing the issue of the Glyphosate in terms of the directions given by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court and the issue is sub-judice. Presently an expert group has been constituted by PPA to conduct a scientific evaluation and examination of all the new evidence/recent submissions made by the Pesticides Associations inter-alia on the issue of the use of Glyphosate.
474.decision: RC perused the report submitted by the Expert group and after detailed scientific deliberations, also recalls that the issue has been dealt by the RC in its various past meetings which are the matter of records. RC is of the considered view that in view of the precautionary principle governing the issue, the use of Glyphosate is required to be restricted through PCO’s and the RC could not find any cogent scientific justifications for continued use of Glyphosate without any restrictions. RC therefore decided that the use of Glyphosate should be restricted and the same may be carried out through trained personnel’s/ PCOs to avoid any risk of occupational hazards and to prevent its misuse. RC directs the Secretary of CIB&RC to communicate this decision to DA&FW for taking an appropriate final view in the matter.

474.title: Gazette Notification dated 08.07.2026 issued by the Central Govt amending the Insecticides Rules 1971 mandating the requirement of an import permit for non- insecticidal uses.
474.decision: RC perused the Gazette Notification dated 08.07.2026 issued by the Central Govt (DA&FW) amending the Insecticides Rules 1971 called as the Insecticides Third Amendment Rules 2026 stipulating the requirement of an import permit for non- insecticidal uses. RC observed that the notification is statutory in nature and has a force of Law and therefore is required to be adhered by all the applicants desiring to import any of the substance included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act, 1968, for non-insecticidal purposes. RC therefore in supersession of all its earlier decision on the subject of import permit decided to comply with the notification dated 08.07.2026. RC also observed that the said notification includes the Form in which an application for grant of permission for import of insecticides for non-insecticidal use is to be made. RC decided that henceforth all the applications are to be made in the stipulated Form and the said notification is required to be put in public domain for information and compliance of all the stakeholders immediately. The finalized guidelines and Form are attached as Annexure-3.2.1. It was further decided that the applications of import permit pending in the Sectt. of CIB&RC shall also be dealt in accordance with revised guidelines with the then application form. RC also directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to issue a public notice to this effect along with an appropriate guideline, forms approved by the RC as notified. A communication shall also be issued to the Custom Authorities for their information and compliance. RC also perused the communication received from M/s Supreme Petrochem Ltd. dated 24.07.2026 regarding the applicability of the Hon’ble Gujarat High Court Order dated 19.11.2025 wherein the requirement of import permit has been set aside to the extent of acrylonitrile to be imported for non-insecticidal use. RC deliberated upon the same and observes that since now the import permit requirement has been stipulated in the Insecticide Rules, 1971 by the way of the Gazette notification dated 08.07.2026 and therefore the requirement of obtaining an import permit is now a statutory requirement and therefore is required to be complied by all applicants for any of the substances proposed to be imported for non-insecticidal uses including acrylonitrile. Secretariat of CIB&RC is directed to communicate M/s Supreme Petrochem Ltd accordingly. RC feels expedient that this decision may also be communicated to DGFT, the regulatory authority vested with the powers of framing the policy pertaining the imports/exports under Ministry of Commerce under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 for information and further needful in the matter.

474.title: Clarification required for the application submitted by M/s Saraswati Agro Chemicals (India).
474.decision: RC deliberated the agenda regarding the application of M/s Saraswati Agro Chemicals (India) Pvt. Ltd. for registration of Formetanate Hydrochloride 20% SP (Formetanate Hydrochloride 23.3% w/w) for formulation indigenous manufacture under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968. The Committee noted that the toxicity studies submitted in support of the proposed formulation had been conducted using test materials differing in active ingredient concentration, study period, sponsors, test facilities and batches. In particular, the active ingredient concentration of the test materials ranged from approximately 10% to 93%, which does not correspond to the proposed formulation containing 23.3% w/w Formetanate Hydrochloride and is not consistent with the principles of toxicological equivalence under the FAO/WHO Manual on Development and Use of Pesticide Specifications and the applicable Indian regulatory framework. The Committee further observed that the Certificates of Analysis and supporting documents submitted were insufficient to establish the identity and equivalence of the tested materials with the proposed formulation. It was also noted that the acute oral toxicity study was not conducted in accordance with the applicable OECD Test Guideline, the acute dermal toxicity study had been conducted on the technical material instead of the proposed formulation, and adequate documentary evidence authorizing reliance on studies generated by different sponsors had not been furnished. In the absence of adequate scientific justification and supporting evidence establishing the equivalence of the tested materials with the proposed formulation, the Committee observed that the submitted toxicological data package does not adequately establish the safety profile of the proposed formulation. Accordingly, the Committee decided that the applicant be invited to make a detailed presentation before the RC in the next meeting to justify the scientific validity and regulatory acceptability of the submitted toxicological data.

474.title: Consideration of Request for technical presentation by M/s. Trical soil Solutions India Pvt. Ltd. regarding Chloropicrin.
474.decision: RC noted the request of M/s Trical Soil Solutions India Pvt. Ltd. seeking an opportunity to make a technical presentation regarding Chloropicrin. After detailed deliberation, and in line with its earlier decision, the Committee observed that Chloropicrin is an intrinsically highly hazardous soil fumigant and a highly volatile compound with severe acute toxicity. The Committee noted that Chloropicrin is a potent irritant to the eyes, skin and respiratory tract, capable of causing severe pulmonary injury, including chemical pneumonitis and delayed pulmonary oedema following inhalation exposure. The Committee further observed that repeated exposure may result in chronic respiratory impairment and systemic toxicity affecting vital organs. The Committee also noted its historical use as a chemical warfare agent and that, owing to its hazardous toxicological profile, its use in countries where it is permitted is subject to stringent regulatory restrictions, including strict occupational exposure limits and risk mitigation measures. Accordingly, the Committee did not agree to the request for a technical presentation and reiterated that the hazards associated with Chloropicrin decisively outweigh its potential benefits and, therefore, its registration is not warranted in India. 10.34 Decision taken by the registration committee at agenda item no. 10.7 in the 453 RC meeting regarding closure of user accounts and shifting to freezed category for non-replying to deficiency raised for more than two months in the KYC module. Whereas the draft rules further to amend the Insecticides Rules, 1971, was published, as required by section 36 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 (46 of 1968), vide notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare) number G.S.R. 855 (E), dated the 18th November, 2025, and published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i), dated the 19th November, 2025, inviting objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be affected thereby, before the expiry of a period of thirty days from the date on which the copies of the Official Gazette in which the said notification was published, were made available to the public; And whereas, copies of the said notification were made available to the public on 19th day of November, 2025; And whereas, objections or suggestions received from the public in respect of the said draft rules have been considered by the Central Government; Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 36 of the said Act, the Central Government hereby makes the following rules further to amend the Insecticides Rules, 1971, namely:- 1. Short title and Commencement.- (1) These rules may be called the Insecticides Third (Amendment) Rules, 2026. (2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 2. In the Insecticides Rules, 1971 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), in rule 4, after clause (b), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:- (6) - (4) 4-6 - [ II 3(i)] 3. In the said rules, after Chapter III, the following Chapter shall be inserted, namely:- MANNER OF IMPORT OF AN INSECTICIDE FOR NON-INSECTICIDAL PURPOSE 8A. Manner of import.- (1) An application for import of an insecticide for non-insecticidal purpose shall be made to the Registration Committee in Form IA. (2) The application under sub-rule (1) shall be accompanied by a fee of rupees five thousand only. (3) The Registration Committee shall have the power to conduct an enquiry to verify the information furnished by the applicant. (4) An application which is complete in all respect shall be considered and disposed by the Registration Committee preferably within a period of forty-five days which may further extend to a period not later than fifteen days. (5) The import permit granted under sub-rule (4) shall be valid for one year. 473.title: Compliance with the Order dated 12.06.2026 of the Hon’ble Revisional Authority regarding re-examination of the issues raised w.r.t the application of M/s Agrow Allied ventures Private Limited for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5 % min. u/s 9(3) TIM vs TI of the Insecticides Act, 1968.
473.decision: RC perused the Order dated 12.06.2026 passed by the Hon'ble Revisional Authority whereas the matter had been remanded by the Hon'ble Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 Revisional Authority for a limited review of the issues relating to the manufacturing process, impurity profile and any potential toxicological implications arising therefrom. RC also perused the letter dated 22.06.2026 from M/s Godrej Agrovet ltd. The Committee was apprised that, in compliance with the directions of the Hon'ble Revisional Authority, the complete chemistry dossier and all documents available on record were re-examined. The Committee noted that the applicant had submitted the requisite documents prescribed under the extant TIM vs. TI Guidelines, including the list of raw materials and intermediates with source of supply, stepwise manufacturing process, chemical equations, flow sheet diagram from raw materials to the final technical product, effluent treatment method, specifications, method of analysis, impurity profile and supporting analytical data. The Committee further noted that chemical equivalence had already been established with the registered source, M/s Godrej Agrovet Limited, and that the chemical composition, specifications and impurity limits submitted by the applicant were identical to those of the registered source. The Committee also noted that an in-process sample drawn during inspection by officers of the Directorate had been tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory (CIL) and found to conform to the submitted specifications. The CIL analysis did not reveal any unidentified impurity or any additional impurity having any toxicological concern. The reported impurity profile was within the prescribed limits and no toxicologically significant impurity arising from the disclosed manufacturing process was detected. The Committee further deliberated upon the concerns raised before the Hon'ble Revisional Authority regarding the manufacturing process and the possible formation of toxicologically significant impurities. After examining the chemistry dossier, impurity profile, CIL analytical report and other material available on record, the Committee observed that no chemistry-related deficiency or safety concern has been established. The available data do not indicate the formation or presence of any additional toxicologically significant impurity under the disclosed manufacturing process. Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 The RC also noted that the petitioner's contention regarding the use of chloroform during the manufacturing process, including the alleged possibility of the formation of isocyanides and it’s derivatives or any other additional impurities arising therefrom, is not revealed from the technical dossier or the reports available on record. The Committee observed that no such concerns are reflected in the technical documentation or analytical reports submitted by the applicant or generated by the Central Insecticides Laboratory. Accordingly, the RC found no merit or substance in the averments made by the petitioner in this regard. Accordingly, the Registration Committee, after thorough re-examination of the matter in compliance with the Order dated 12.06.2026 of the Hon'ble Revisional Authority and considering the available material on records, found no reason to interfere with its earlier decision taken in the 470th RC Meeting under Agenda Item No. 6.54, to grant registration for the indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5% Min. under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968, in the TIM vs. TI category, to M/s Agrow Allied Ventures Private Limited. The Committee, therefore, decided to uphold its earlier decision for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5% Min. under Section 9(3) (TIM vs TI) to M/s Agrow Allied Ventures Private Limited, with a provisional shelf life of two years based on Accelerated Storage Stability (ASS) data, in accordance with the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.48). The applicant shall submit real- time shelf-life data within two and a half years from the date of submission of the application, failing which the Registration Certificate shall be deemed cancelled. The existing condition shall continue to form part of the Certificate of Registration. RC directs the Secretary, CIB&RC to communicate this decision to the Hon’ble Revisional Authority and the respective Parties.

473.title: Judgement dated 29.05.2026 passed by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court in LPA No 215/2023, Dhanuka Agritech Limited v/s Union of India & Ors. Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026
473.decision: RC perused the Judgement dated 29.05.2026 passed by Division Bench of the Hon’ble Delhi High Court in the above matter and observed that the impugned decisions of the RC taken in its 430th meeting and as amended in 431st meeting granting registration for the import of Halosulfuron Methyl Technical 98% min. and Halosulfuron Methyl 75% WG formulation to M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited, has been quashed/ set aside. RC also observes that in compliance with the said judgement conveyed by the Union Counsel, the Secretariat of CIB&RC had already written a communication dated 11.06.2026 to M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited to surrender the original captioned CRs forthwith to the Secretariat of CIB&RC and shall not utilize the same for any purposes whatsoever. The copy of said communication dated 11.06.2026 had also been sent to the respective State Director of Agriculture for taking further appropriate steps in accordance with law. RC also perused an email communication dated 17.06.2026 from M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited wherein they have informed that they have approached the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India by special leave petition (SLP) challenging the judgement dated 29.05.2026 wherein Union of India and CIB&RC are also arrayed as a party respondent. They have thus assured that they shall not act upon and utilize the above CRs and had requested for a reasonable time to surrender the captioned original certificates pending the initial hearing of the SLP. RC deliberated the issues and is of the considered view that since the decision of the RC taken in its 430th and 431st meeting has been set aside by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide its judgement dated 29.05.2026 and therefore, the same is required to be complied in its true letter and spirit. RC is also of the view that all consequential approvals/ permissions granted by the State Governments also does not survive. RC thus decided that the applicant may be directed to immediately and forthwith surrender the original CRs for the above products to the Secretariat of CIB&RC without any fail. RC also directs the Secretariat of CIB&RC to issue an appropriate communication to the respective State Governments to revoke the manufacturing licenses granted for the captioned CRs and/ or any other action required to be taken in this regard in accordance with law. Further, it was reiterated that the above decision of the RC shall be subject to any of the directions that may be passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the Special Leave Petition filed by M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited. RC also directs the Secretary, CIB&RC to take all necessary steps to appropriately deal with the matter including seeking of any inputs/assistance required from the concerned technical experts who had dealt with the matter.

473.decision: The RC deliberated the agenda and re-iterated its earlier decision regarding of import of CRMs in its 470th meeting vide agenda item No. 10.29. It added the following: 1. It may be noted that Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) which may include banned and/or restricted pesticides are analytical standards used exclusively for testing, calibration, method validation, quality control, and standardization purposes in laboratories. These materials are imported Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 and utilized in very small quantities and are not intended for commercial use, formulation, manufacturing, sale, distribution, or field application. Considering their limited quantity and specialized use in analytical and research activities, the Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIB&RC) has exempted the import of Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) from the requirement of obtaining import permission under the provisions administered by CIB&RC. Stakeholders may therefore import CRMs intended solely for research and development purposes, laboratory testing, calibration, validation, and standardization activities to be carried out in Research and development Laboratories/Centers, testing and calibration laboratories, etc. for testing of pesticides, without obtaining prior import permission from CIB&RC. Keeping this in view, importers are advised to maintain adequate records demonstrating that the imported materials are Certified Reference Materials and are being used exclusively for the aforesaid purposes. For the import of chemicals and laboratory reagents which are included in the schedule of the Insecticides Act, 1968, the RC has directed Secretary, CIB&RC to arrange for a joint meeting with DCPC, DGFT, Customs and FSSAI to gauge the situation, and discuss present issues. The proceedings and minutes of the meeting and any decisions thereof shall be presented to the RC for further consideration and review.
