472.title: Presentation by M/s. FMC India Pvt. Ltd. The representatives of applicant made a detailed presented on all the four issues related to the new molecule Tetflupyrolimet technical.
472.decision: After detailed deliberations it was decided as under: i) Purity: RC noted that CSF submitted by applicant is not yet accepted in USEPA and the molecule is not registered in the country of its origin i.e. USA. In view thereof, applicant may please comply with the recommendations of in-house group on “Establishment of minimum purity in India based on the registration of technical active ingredient by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA)” as accepted in 421st RC meeting vide agenda item 3.1. ii) Committee accepted the contention of applicant on DHODH and PFAS. iii) The RC decided that as per the decision of 421st RC a Standard Deviation tolerance limit shall be applicable to the 97% minimum purity applied by their parent company in USA. The minimum purity is arrived at 94.624% min. iv) Therefore, the RC decided that the purity of Tetflupyrolimet technical shall be 94.6% minimum plus impurities to make chemical composition 100.00%. v) It was also emphasised that all the data submitted by the applicant such as ATR & Shelf-Life etc shall be according to Tetflupyrolimet technical as 94.6% minimum. The sample under PRV shall also be conforming to the requirement of Tetflupyrolimet technical as 94.6% minimum. It was also decided that if, the applicant accepts the above said decision, then the applicant has to give in writing for accepting the above decision along-with revised Form-I, MOA, Product Specification in consonance of Tetflupyrolimet technical 94.6% minimum. The representatives of the applicant presented that Based on the weight of evidence approach, there was no evidence of adverse effects on immune system components in short-term (28- and 90-day) studies in rats, mice and dogs, or in long-term studies in rats and mice. These endpoints included WBC parameters, thymus weights, gross and histopathology of thymus, lymph nodes, and bone marrow. Further, applicant presented the interpretation (extract from EPA document Part158) as below: • Hemosiderin deposits of the spleen may occur secondary to hemorrhage or hemolysis that is unrelated to direct immunotoxicity. • Spleen congestion (passive accumulation of blood) may result from non-immune toxic effects such as hemolytic anemia or barbiturate euthanasia. • Extramedullary hematopoiesis of the spleen is commonly seen in rodents (particularly mice) in the absence of underlying disease and can be indicative of anemia/hemorrhage/hemolysis, systemic inflammation, splenic trauma/necrosis, decreased hematopoiesis by the bone marrow, and neoplasia. • Spleen histopathological changes in the absence of other lesion are unlikey to be specific indicator of immunotoxicity. Additionally, expected dietary exposure levels are very low with margin of exposure more than 10 million. Hence, Applicant concluded “In view of observation and sufficient scientific weight of evidence (WoE) to conclude that Tetflupyrolimet does not have potential for immunotoxicity.” RC further noted the below facts: 1. Tetflupyrolimet is first and only new mode of action (MOA-DHODH Inhibitor) herbicide being introduced in over 30 years. 2. Immunotoxicity study is the mandatory data requirement for 9(3)TI new molecule as per extant guidelines to assess the overall safety of human being. 3. Toxicology data on tetflupyrolimet is being extensively debated, assessed and has not been accepted in USEPA till date. RC was further apprised with “A Retrospective Analysis of the Immunotoxicity Study (OCSPP Test Guideline No. 870. 7800)” published by USEPA dated February, 2013 wherein below was opined: “Traditional subchronic and chronic rodent studies can provide some information on certain immunological endpoints such as hematology, lymphoid organ weights and histopathology. Nonetheless, EPA concluded in 2007 that these endpoints alone do not provide a full and integrated evaluation of immune function. Evaluating the potential of a chemical to adversely affect the immune system function is important because immune system suppression has been associated with increased incidences of diseases. Accordingly, that year the Agency revised the Part 158 Toxicology Data requirements to require a functional immunotoxicity study for all food and non-food use pesticides.” In view thereof, RC decided that member toxicologist Dr Umesh D. Surrangi may assess the requirement of immunotoxicity study, so that a final an appropriate decision may be taken, since he was not present in the meeting.

472.title: Presentation by M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd. In terms of the RC decision taken in its 468th RC meeting, at agenda item no. 10.2 in relation to representation of Non verification of registration certificate of M/s Meghmani Industries Ltd. Ahmedabad wherein
472.decision: RC decided to invite the applicant for presentation before the RC. The decision of the RC read as under: “RC perused the agenda and expressed its serious concern on the issue of possessing of forged/fake certificate of registration for Sulphur 80% WDG purported to be issued vide Registration No. CIR- 69,758/2005(254)-Sulphur (WDG-1125) from F. No. 1,372-F 9(4)/2005 by M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad. The issue came to light when the company moved an application for the attestation of this certificate of registration and on being enquired about the genuineness of the same from available records at Sectt. of CIB&RC it was revealed that the above file no. doesn’t pertain to any such application for the grant of registration submitted by the M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad. Further the CR records that the above registration was approved by the RC in its 254th meeting on the contrary no such approval was found in the entire MOM of 254th meeting. Prima-facie RC is of the view that M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad is utilizing the above-mentioned CR which apparently appears to be fake and forged and, in any event, couldn’t be presumed as genuine. Such type of illegal activities is to be checked at the threshold with exemplary punishments to the wrong doers. RC still is inclined to grant an opportunity to show cause M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad before taking any further view in the matter. RC directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC to call M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad to submit their point of view on the above aspect in the next RC.”. The applicant appeared before the RC along with their Learned Counsel Sh. Ashish Kothari Advocate, during the course of RC proceedings the applicant has submitted a presentation document which is taken on record. Mr. Kothari submits that the applicant is a leading group engaged in manufacture of agrochemicals for more than four decades and enjoy a good reputation between the farmers due to its quality products. He further submits that the applicant is a law-abiding company and is committed to ensure all regulatory compliances. Mr Kothari further submits that the captioned RC of Sulphur 80% WDG has been issued around twenty years back and that point of time the applications were used to be submitted in hard copy mode and the CRs are also received in physical hard copy form. He submits that the captioned CR bears the signature of the then Secretary CIB&RC and also contains the official stamp and therefore the applicant was using the same under the bona- fide belief that the same is genuine. Mr. Kothari also submits that since then several endorsement and certification have been sought by the applicant and the same were granted by the RC on several occasions and no question was raised as to the lack of genuineness of the said CR. He also refers Section 51, 52 and 78 of the Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 which inter-alia relates to the presumptions as to genuineness of the certified copies. However, on instructions, he fairly states that since the question has been raised about the lack of genuineness of the captioned CR., and in full bona-fides they are ready and willing to surrender the original CR to the RC, with a liberty to reapply of the registration of the same as per the applicable guidelines. Now after hearing the submissions, the RC deliberated upon the same and is of the considered view that any sort of illegality as and when detected is to be thrown out at any stage. Since the applicant had made a fair submission and is ready to surrender the original CR and therefore the RC is of the view that the submissions so advanced by Mr. Kothari the Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant deserves consideration. Accordingly, RC directs the applicant to submit an affidavit on NJSP to this effect duly sweared in accordance with law under the signatures of the authorized person not below the rank of the Director of the Company with the original CR along with the all-consequential original endorsements/certifications received by the applicant, to the Secretariat of CIB&RC with copy of the same duly endorsed to the respective State Director of Agriculture/s and duly acknowledged by them. Sr. Law Officer is also requested to verify the contents of the affidavit so submitted by the applicant in view of the submissions/statements made in the presentation document. RC makes it clear that if any such instance is found in future and/or comes to the notice of the RC, serious legal consequences shall entail.

472.title: Templates/Proforma for the scrutiny of the applications of registration of pesticides in various category.
472.decision: The RC recalled its decision taken in the 468th RC meeting held on 12.01.2026 vide Agenda Item No. 3.2, wherein the draft templates developed by the Sectt. of CIB&RC for speedy examination of applications under various categories of registration within the stipulated time were approved for inviting comments/suggestions from stakeholders. The RC noted that, in compliance with its earlier decision, the Sectt. of CIB&RC issued a Public Notice dated 12.02.2026 inviting comments/suggestions from stakeholders on the draft templates. The RC further noted that meetings with stakeholders were held on 06.03.2026 and 08.05.2026, wherein the comments/suggestions received were deliberated and subsequently compiled for consideration by the RC. All the comments and suggestion given by the various Stake holders such Pesticides Associations, individual applicants etc have been incorporated in the template. The revised and corrected templates were deliberated in details in view of the regulatory requirements of Chemistry, Toxicology, Chemistry, Packaging and Bio-efficacy (Herbicide Unit) etc. The RC observed that some of the pages are missing in the template. The same was presented by the Secretary to the RC. After detailed perusal and deep discussion RC finalized the revised templates for implementation. The RC further decided that these templates shall be made integral part of the guidelines in the CROP portal, so that it becomes the mandatory requirement of submission by the applicant at the time of filling an application of registration. It was further decided that, once incorporated in the Crop Portal no application shall be accepted without information in the respective templates under all disciplines as per the approved guidelines. RC also further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a public notice on the website and addressing to the Pesticides Associations; requesting to encourage their members to come forward and submit the information in template in an endeavour to grant of registration speedily. It was also expected that the existing applicant shall also be given an opportunity to join in this endeavour to expedite scrutiny and analysis of data, if they want the scrutiny of their files at fast pace. After detailed deliberations, the RC approved the templates. The revised and approved templates, in sync with the Guidelines, are annexed at Annexure 3.2.1, for implementation by the Sectt. of CIB&RC.

472.title: Consideration of an application of M/s Bayer CropScience Limited for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Isoxaflutole Technical 97.2% w/w Min under section 9(3) TI of the Insecticides Act, 1968.
472.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and approved the case of M/s Bayer Crop Science Limited for grant of registration of Isoxaflutole Technical 97.2% w/w min under import category subject to submission of toxicology data on major and persistent metabolites found in soil i.e RPA 202248 (Diketonitrile- Primary Metabolite) and RPA 203328(IFT-Benzoic acid- Terminal metabolite) & an undertaking on variation in Address of source of Import on RTT permit and consent letter and submission of revised form-I with complete address of source of Import as complete address is not mentioned on Form-I and original hard-copy Affidavit / ICAMA / Consent (Apostille/Legalized) with geo tagging of manufacturing source, whichever is applicable, if not already submitted. The applicant has submitted that the address in RTT and consent letter differs because of “one address belongs to the office address and another address belongs to the manufacturing address of the same source”. The validity of product is 31st July, 2034. RC deliberated the agenda extensively and it was emerged that the major metabolites of isoxaflutole are persistent, mobile in soil and prone to leaching and accumulation in ground water leading to water contamination. It was also noted that Diketonitrile is the major and active herbicidal metabolite.

472.title: Consideration of an application of M/s Willowood Chemicals Ltd., for grant of registration of Haloxyfop-p-Methyl Technical 95.00 % w/w Min. for TI-(New Source) u/s 9(3) of the Insecticide Act, 1968.
472.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and noted that Haloxyfop-p-Methyl and Haloxyfop-R-Methyl Ester refer to the same highly effective, selective post- emergence racemic herbicide. The 'R' and 'P' denote its chemical configuration as the active enantiomer, making it twice as potent as the older, unresolved mixture of isomers. Haloxyfop molecules are chiral, meaning they can exist in two mirror-image forms: the R-enantiomer and the S-enantiomer. These specify the R-enantiomer, which is the biologically active form that actually kills weeds. The original herbicide was simply called haloxyfop-methyl, it was a 50/50 mix of both the active (R) and inactive (S) forms. Haloxyfop-p-methyl CAS no. is 72619-32-0 & Haloxyfop-R-methyl CAS no. is also 72619-32-0, hence synonyms. The MSDS of Haloxyfop-R-methyl is attached as annexure-6.71.1. The product is already registered in the name of Haloxyfop-R-Methyl Ester Technical 94% w/w min. u/s 9(3)-TI is registered in favour of M/s Dow AgroSciences India (P) Ltd vide agenda item 6.5 of 429th RC meeting held in June 2021 in the country. Since this applicant company and the source of import are different and the purity is more, therefore, Haloxyfop-p-Methyl Technical 95.00 % w/w Min. may be entertained for TI-(New Source) u/s 9(3), subject to submission of a satisfactory clarification why they shall not be issued the registration in the name of Haloxyfop-R-methyl technical. After affirmative submission of clarification of above concern raised by the RC, applicant has to submit information/documents as per extended guidelines approved in 468th & 470th RC meeting such as apostille /notarized copy of application form containing Chemical Composition submitted to the regulatory authority in the exporting country with a undertaking by the source that their source can be cancelled without any notice, if their Chemical Composition is found different from the registered one at the time of registration, and submission of the original hard-copy Affidavit / ICAMA / Consent (Apostilled/Legalized) with geo tagging of manufacturing source, whichever is applicable, if not already submitted.

472.title: Consideration of the request from M/s FIL Industries Private Limited for the endorsement of change of corporate office address from H-88, The South Mall, South Extension-1, New Delhi-110049 To Plot No. 23, Local Shopping Centre, Near Pushpa Bhawan, Madangir, New Delhi- 110062 in respect of 02 Nos. of Registration Certificates.
472.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that the applicant has applied for the endorsement for change of its office address and being a private limited company, a query was raised to provide the proof of change of company’s address from the ROC. In the response submitted by the applicant it was pointed out that there is no specific requirement under the Companies Act, 2013 for the filing of such a requirement in case of change in corporate office and such requirement only applies if the registered office address is changed. RC also observed that the applicant has not referred to any specific provision which may indicate as such. RC also further observed that such submission of proof is required under the RC guidelines/checklist which are statutory in nature and the same are required to be adhered to. RC feels that any change in any place, it shall be obvious that such changes may also be notified to the concerned Statutory Authorities. Even RC is also of the view that in order to satisfy itself any legal documents relevant to the matter may be asked to be submitted by the applicant in order to enable the RC to arrive at a subjective satisfaction before taking a final decision. The applicant had since submitted the utility bill for the premises requested to be endorsed and therefore RC feels that the request may be considered this time to avoid any delay and to facilitate the same. RC accordingly decided to approve the same subject to submission of an affidavit duly sweared in accordance with law as to the genuineness of the submissions made by the applicant with the copy of the same duly endorsed to the State Department of Agriculture to be verified by Sr. Law Officer.

472.title: Clarification regarding applicability of State Verification Letter for unfreezing of user accounts on CROP Portal in cases where no certificate has been obtained by the firm.
472.decision: The Committee deliberated upon the agenda in detail. After examination of the matter, the Committee observed that in cases where a firm/entity had merely created a user account on the CROP Portal but had not obtained any Certificate of Registration, Import Permit, RTT Permit, Free Sale Certificate, or any other approval/document from the Secretariat of CIB&RC, insistence on submission of a State Verification Letter issued by the Directorate of Agriculture may not be necessary for activation/unfreezing of the user account. However, the Committee emphasized that the existence and operational status of the firm/entity should be duly authenticated before activation of such accounts. Accordingly, the Committee decided that, in lieu of the State Verification Letter issued by the Directorate of Agriculture of the concerned State, the applicant firm/entity shall submit documentary proof issued by GST authorities or any other Government office/competent authority {Pollution Control Board, State Industrial Development Corporation/Industrial Area Development Authority, District Industries Centre (DIC), Directorate of Industries/Department of Industries or any other Central/State Government Department or statutory authority maintaining records of operational business establishments} which can authenticate that the business establishment/site is genuine, operational, and functional. The Committee further decided that such requests for activation/unfreezing of user accounts may be processed subject to completion of prescribed KYC requirements and submission of requisite documents as prescribed at the Secretariat level only. In all other cases, the decision taken by the RC in its 471st Meeting held on 16.04.2026 under Agenda Item No. 10.26 regarding mandatory submission of State Verification Letter shall continue to remain applicable.

472.title: Request submitted by M/s. Syngenta India Ltd. for the consideration of application for the registration of Thiamethoxam 12.6 % + Lambda cyhalothrin 9.5 % ZC for the control of House insect pests under label expansion category of the Insecticides Act, 1968
472.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in detail on the justification proffered by the applicant. The RC observed that the proposed product has already been registered for the control of insect pests in various agricultural crops and not for the control of House Hold (HH) insect pests. This issue was also discussed in the last RC meeting too for the requirement of data on Health Monitoring studies, which is not a requirement under agriculture usage. The above study is a mandatory requirement for grant of registration under HH category. This requirement is also applicable to the label expansion cases for HH category pesticides. The submission of the applicant that the proposed product was already approved for use in various crops like cotton, maize, groundnut, soybean, chilli, tea, tomato etc. is not tenable as the purpose and usage of the proposed formulation is not for use in agriculture and consequentially the purpose has been changed and therefore the said data is inherently required to ensure the safety of human beings. The RC further noted that the Protocol of conducting the Health Monitoring Studies has been proposed by the Sectt. of CIB&RC in the present RC meeting itemised at agenda 10.51 and the same has been approved specifying the parameters for its applicability on house hold (HH) products. The requirement of seeking approval of protocol on each occasion of HH has been dispensed with immediate effect. Therefore, the applicant may be communicated that the data on Health Monitoring Studies to be generated as per prevailing guidelines and submit the same alongwith their application in appropriate category. In the present matter RC observes that as the application has been submitted with incomplete data, thus the RC decided to close the application and suggest the applicant to apply afresh with all requisite data of HH category. The scrutiny comments of the concerned expert shall be considered during processing of the fresh application and only new study shall be scrutinized as and when submitted again.

472.title: Follow up action on Agenda Item No. 10.16 of 470th RC Meeting decision w.r.t Representation by PMFAI with a request for clarification regarding selling of Technical Grade pesticides and requirement of license to sell technical in states other than the state where the manufacturing plant located.
472.decision: RC perused the agenda and taking into the account the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971, it becomes apparent that the Insecticides Act, 1968 was enacted to regulate import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution, and use of insecticides with a view to preventing risk to human beings, animals and the environment per se. RC also observes that the said legislation creates a centralized registration mechanism for insecticides; and decentralized licensing and concurrent enforcement of quality control mechanisms through Central and State authorities. RC also observes that registration granted under the Act is Pan-India in character. Section 9 of the Act provides for registration of insecticides by the Registration Committee constituted under the Act. Once an insecticide is registered under Section 9, such registration is not confined to any particular State. The registration so granted, permits manufacture and sale of the product throughout India subject to compliance with the Act and Rules. Accordingly, RC notes that the statutory focus is upon the registration of the product by the RC and licensing of the manufacturing premises/activity by the respective State Governments. A manufacturing license authorizes production from the licensed premises. Separate sale licenses may be required for dealers, retailers, distributors, or Stockists etc. operating from commercial premises in any State. However, such sale licensing requirements applicable to dealers or distributors etc. cannot be conflated with the manufacturer’s license. RC is of the view that if the manufacturer appoints distributors or depots in another State, the relevant entity handling sale/storage operations may require the appropriate sale license under the applicable regulatory framework. Nevertheless, the manufacturer himself is not required to obtain a fresh/separate manufacturing license /permission merely because the goods move inter-State. and therefore, a manufacturer holding a valid manufacturing license for its insecticide manufacturing unit in any one State is not required to obtain another manufacturing license/permission separately, merely for supplying or distributing its products in any other State. Accordingly, RC is of the considered view that a duly licensed manufacturer may lawfully supply its insecticide products across India, subject to compliance with applicable sale/distribution licensing requirements for downstream channels. RC observed that being a policy matter the concurrence of DA&FW is required and therefore the RC directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to communicate this decision to DA&FW for consideration and concurrence before its implementation and issue of public notice to this effect.

472.title: Follow up action on the 470th RC decision at Agenda Item No. 10.15 w.r.t representation by Agrochemical Manufacturers Association of India, Gujarat on the issue of “marketed by” arrangements.
472.decision: RC perused the agenda and observe that although the RC had dealt similar issues in its 461st Meeting at Agenda Item No. 10.5 which reads as under: “Clarification on inclusion of marketing agency in manufacturing license and issuing NOC for additional factory address RC perused the communication received from the state department of Karnataka inter- alia asking for a clarification regarding the endorsement of marketing agencies. The state government has quoted rule 20 of the Insecticides Rule which they have submitted that any alteration in the label and leaflets requires permission from the Registration Committee. RC deliberated the agenda in light of the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971 and observed that the grant of licenses for manufacture, sale, transport, distribution etc. lies in the domain of the respective State Governments and RC also observed that any consequential changes w.r.t. the change in the marketing agencies may be made by the state government after due satisfaction to them. Further, any provision of the Act does not preclude the State authorities to carry out such amendments which does not substantially impact the conditions of the CR. Furthermore, the Rule 20 provides that any alteration of any inscription or mark, made on the container, label or wrapper of any insecticide may be made at the instance, direction or permission of the Registration Committee. In view of this Registration Committee hence permits the endorsement of the marketing agencies by the state government under the title “Marketed by” of the label as prescribed under the Insecticides Rules after due satisfaction to them following the prescribed procedure and abiding to rest of the conditions approved by the RC for a pesticide. RC directed Secretariat of CIB&RC to communicate the same to concerned pesticides Associations.” RC notes that a communication had been received from DA&FW vide email communication dated 12.03.2026 forwarding a letter/representation dated 06.03.2026 from Bhartiya Kisan Union requesting the complete abolition of Marketed by system by Pesticides companies and providing quality pesticides to farmers. RC observes that a communication was sent by the Secretary, CIB&RC on 15.05.2026 to DA&FW apprising the 461st RC decision (Agenda 10.5) along with the fact that the issues are under examination in terms of 470th RC decision (Agenda 10.15) and the RC shall take a final appropriate view in the matter. Now therefore, RC proceeds to examine the permissibility of a Separate Marketing agency/company for Insecticides. It is gathered that as per common practice in India, one manufacturer may be manufacturing a particular product for several other companies under their respective brand names for marketing purposes. RC looked into the Statutory Framework under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971, which expressly contemplate a distinction between the manufacturer and the marketer/vendor of insecticide products. RC perused Rule 19 of the Insecticides Rules, 1971 (dealing with labelling requirements) which mandates that the label of every insecticide package must contain, among other particulars the name and address of the manufacturer; and the name of the marketer. RC observes that this dual-declaration requirement demonstrates that the regulatory scheme anticipates and permits marketing arrangements. Since the domain of licensing lies with the State Governments and therefore the focal point of satisfaction lies with the State w.r.t. the issues pertaining to marketing agencies. RC is of the view that the States should also ensure that the manufacturers and /or marketers should not escape from legal consequences in case of any violations committed under the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules 1971. RC, thus, recognizes that concept of marketing agencies is legaland permissible under the applicable statutory framework, provided all registration and licensing requirements under the Statute are duly complied with. RC is of the view that being a policy matter the guidance and concurrence of DA&FW is also required and therefore the RC directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to communicate this decision to DA&FW for consideration and concurrence before its implementation.

471.title: The Registration Committee (RC) recalled its decision taken in its 469th meeting under Agenda item no, 3.1 wherein the RC sought geo-tagging details of the manufacturing location of the source of import in overseas country. The RC observed that geo-tagging details, duly legalized/apostilled by the competent authority of the respective country, may be considered as proof of the manufacturing location, along with a location map indicating the place where manufacturing activities are carried out. The Registration Committee (RC) recalled its earlier decisions taken in its 469th meeting under Agenda Item No. 3.1 and 470th meeting under Agenda Item No. 8.2, wherein the RC had sought geo-tagging details of the manufacturing location in the overseas country.
471.decision: The RC decided that the geo-tagging details, duly legalized/apostilled by the competent authority of the respective country, may be considered as valid proof of the manufacturing location. Such submission should be Minutes of 471st RC meeting held on 16.04.2026 accompanied by a location map indicating the precise place of manufacturing; indicating the site where the manufacturing activities are being carried out. The RC further decided that the Geo-tagging of all the registrant shall be obtained irrespective of import or indigenous. The geo tagging shall be made the part of requirement of all the guidelines for uniformly implementation and accurate locations. All the applicant should submit geo-tagging details once this feature is made live on CROP portal. CGG may be requested to develop this feature urgently.

Scientific Redundancy in Crop Trial Requirements 3. Practical Constraints Relating to RTT Requirement
471.decision: RC deliberated the matter and observed that after a series of detailed deliberations made in 467th, 468th & 470th meeting; the RC had already considered the suggestions made by the stake holders and therefore RC don’t find any cogent reason to modify or amend the guidelines captioned in the matter pertaining to the TI-New Source as the requirements laid down are fully scientifically justified and RC expects its compliance from all the stake holders so as to ensure availability of safer and quality pesticides to the farmers. As far as the applicability of the captioned guidelines is concerned, RC in its 470th meeting has already clarified that the additional data requirements shall be implemented for all applications. RC is further of the view that the persons who had obtained a RTT permit for the purposes of data generation can and should follow the additional data requirements since the application under TI New source is not submitted or pending before the RC. Presentation by M/s T. Stanes and company Ltd. regarding follow up action on Agenda Item No. 10.35 of 469th RC meeting. The representatives of the applicant, M/s T. Stanes and Company Ltd., made a detailed presentation before the RC. After hearing the submissions of the applicant, RC observed that Citral and Geraniol are included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act, 1968. In view of the same, both molecules shall be treated as integral components of the product. The concerned Expert informed that the present application is for grant of registration of Cymbopogan plant extract (containing 1% Geraniol min). It was further elaborated that Cymbopogan plant extract is rich in monoterpenes, specifically citral (α and β), geranial, neral, geraniol, citronellal, and myrcene. It also contains flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic compounds also. It was also observed that Citral has been included in the Schedule to the IA, 1968 vide notification No. S.O. 1854(E) dated 29th April, 2024. As the Citral has been included into the Schedule to the Insecticides Act 1968, hence guidelines of registration and data requirement is applicable. Therefore, the applicant is required to submit complete and updated data for Citral as per guidelines, including the percentage (% w/w) content of Citral in the Chemical Composition (CC) through a revised Form-I, along with Labels/Leaflets (L/Ls) and NJSP. The applicant shall also submit revised Product Specifications specifying the parameters of Citral and Method of Analysis (MOA). All such submissions shall be in accordance with the applicable guidelines and shall be treated as mandatory for further examination by the Registration Committee.
Presentation by M/s Agro Life Science Corporation for consideration of application of Thiodicarb 50 % + Imidacloprid 5 % WDG u/s 9(3) FIM.
470.decision: The Registration Committee deliberated on the presentation made by the applicant in the 470th RC meeting regarding the proposed formulation. As per the 469th RC minutes, the applicant was invited to make a presentation before the Registration Committee in the 470th meeting to justify the absolute necessity for registration of the proposed formulation. The applicant made the presentation before the Committee. After detailed deliberation, the Registration Committee observed that the applicant has not justified in the presentation that the proposed formulation is an absolute necessity for its registration in view of the recommendations of the Dr. C.D. Mayee Committee. The Committee further observed that the combination belongs to the red toxicity triangle category, whereas the individual formulations of each technical do not fall under the red triangle category. Both Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 components are neurotoxicants, and the synergistic effect of the components appears evident. The Committee also noted that safer alternatives are available. The Committee was apprised that if a formulation is more toxic than its technical grade active ingredient, sub-acute toxicity studies are required as per the guidelines and decisions of the Registration Committee (449th RC). Further, the applicant requested to conduct the study again as per OECD 425; however, the Committee was of the view that repeating the study would not add any substantial outcome to the assessment. In view of the above, the Committee concluded that the proposed formulation is not justified for registration and therefore doesn’t qualify for the consideration of grant of registration. Accordingly, the matter is disposed-of.

470.title: Order of Hon’ble appellate authority in appeal no. 12 of 2025 M/s. Drosera International Pvt. Ltd. vs CIB&RC. Fresh revision petition filed by CCFI vs CIB&RC. Representation of ACFI dated 25.02.2026 on the issues of data requirement for 9(3) TI New Source (467th & 468th RC meetings).
470.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that M/s Drosera International Pvt. Ltd. had filed an appeal against the guidelines for TI New Source issued by the RC in its 467th Meeting at agenda item no. 3.2 wherein it was alleged that the said guidelines inter-alia had adversely affected the appellants rights and legitimate expectations. It was also submitted before the appellate authority that the said guidelines were made applicable retrospectively which is not tenable in the eyes of law. The appellate authority after hearing the appellant and the CIB&RC, had found the appeal to be not admissible, recognizing that the power of the RC flows from section 5 of the Insecticide Act with respect to framing, reviewing and modifying the technical guidelines and therefore are not amenable to the Appellate jurisdiction u/s 10 of the Act. However, the liberty has been granted to the appellant to submit a representation before the RC highlighting its technical concerns/difficulties arising from the said guidelines and the RC may consider and examine the same in accordance with the Law and applicable regulatory framework. RC also perused an email communication dated 13.03.2026 received from Dr. Shilpa Arora Advocate, the counsel of the appellant. RC also perused the representation dated 25.02.2026 submitted by M/s ACFI wherein inter-alia it is stated that the certain scientific requirements pertaining to the shelf-life data, bio efficacy, toxicity may be dispensed with and the requirements as per 449th RC meeting be implemented in a balanced and scientifically justified manner. RC after detailed deliberation observed that the guidelines so formulated in its 467th meeting at agenda item no. 3.2 were subsequently modified in its 468th meeting, wherein the waiver has been granted to the livestock metabolism study and the RC is of the view that the requirements so laid down are scientifically and essentially required for the evaluations of safety and efficacy of the substance proposed to be registered under TI New Source and also these guidelines have been made more transparent and clear so that there may not exist any ambiguity in understanding the data requirements to be followed by the applicant. However certain correction in the guidelines as per scientific requirements are made. The revised guideline is attached as Annexure 3.1.1. The same shall be applicable from the date of publishing the minutes on the website. RC also observed that the requirements so laid down are not as such which are unable to be fulfilled by the applicant. In view of the above deliberation, the RC is of the considered view that the requirements laid down are reasonable and scientifically justified. RC is also of the view that data requirements are Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 to be implemented prospectively and shall have no bearing on the existing applications submitted in CROP. Only information is required to be submitted by all the existing/pending applications, extra data required (than existing guidelines) in revised guidelines not to be submitted by the existing applicant. RC also perused the revision petition filled by M/s CCFI on the challenge of the RC decision taken in its 468th meeting at agenda item no 2.2 and agenda item no 1. RC notes that the hearing in the above revision petition has been notified for 06.04.2026 by the Hon’ble Authority. RC directs the concerned technical experts to adequately deal with the matter as appropriate and justified submissions may be made before the Hon’ble Revisional Authority. RC also desired that if any directions are issued by the Hon’ble Authority the same shall be placed before the RC for appropriate compliance.

470.title: Consideration of an application of M/s Agrow Allied Ventures Private Limited, for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5% Min under section 9(3) TIM vs TI.
470.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and also considered the representation received from the Office of the Hon’ble Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare regarding reconsideration of the proposal for grant of registration to M/s Agro Allied Ventures Private Limited for manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical (93.5% w/w minimum) under Section 9(3) in the TIM vs TI category. RC was apprised that the representation, inter alia, raised concerns regarding alleged non- compliance with the TIM vs TI guidelines approved in the 359th RC meeting dated 02.11.2015. The issues highlighted included non-submission of complete stepwise manufacturing process from initial raw materials, possible clubbing of manufacturing steps, non-disclosure of raw materials, intermediates and their sources, absence of detailed flow sheet diagram from Step-I, and concerns regarding incomplete characterization of impurity profile. RC took note of the issues raised in the representation and deliberated upon the same in the context of the data submitted by the applicant and the provisions of the extant guidelines. After detailed deliberation and consideration of the representation, the concerned expert explained that the application is complete from chemistry angle as per the requirement of guidelines, hence RC approved the grant of registration for technical indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical (93.5% w/w minimum) under Section 9(3) [TIM vs TI], with a provisional shelf life of two years, based on the submission of Accelerated Storage Stability (ASS) data, in accordance with the 424th RC decision (Agenda Item No. 10.48). The applicant has to submit the real time shelf-life data as per existing guideline of RC within two and half years of submission of Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 application for granting the registration, failing which Registration Certificate shall be deemed cancelled. A condition shall be incorporated in the CR of the applicant.

470.title: Compliance with 469th RC decision-submission of detailed and verified manufacturing address of the source from the overseas country and Geo tagging along with photographs in case of 9(4) TI/ FI applications. The Registration Committee (RC) recalled its decision taken in the 469th RC meeting under Agenda Item No. 3.1, wherein the RC sought the geo-tagging details of the manufacturing location in the overseas country. The RC further observed that the geo-tagging details, duly legalized/apostilled by the competent authority of the respective country, may be considered as a proof along with a location map indicating the place where the manufacturing activities are carried out in that country. However, RC observed that the issues are further required to be looked into in-depth being pertaining to overseas countries vis a vis the issue related to the acceptance/approval of chemical composition etc.
470.decision: The RC directed the Secretary, CIB&RC that any case put-up to RC should be scientifically and legally justified. In view of above RC directs the concerned Experts to bring a detailed agenda clearly mentioning the earlier RC decision on the subject in consultation with the Senior Law Officer on the legal issues that may be involved.

470.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and observed that there is change in the name of the source of import as well as its address/location etc. The RC apprised that there are various categories of applications received in the Sectt. of CIBRC on the issue as under: 1. Endorsement of change of name of source of Import of chemicals due to disinvestment. 2. Change of name of source of import 3. Change of manufacturing site 4. Addition of manufacturing site It was further observed that checklist exists on the above issues. It was also informed that as per checklist there is no requirement of submission of 5 batch sample to CIL in the existing checklist. Even some of the “case to case basis” RC has asked the applicant to do so. Therefore, the applicant is required to submit 5-batch analysis report as per check list, if already not submitted and 5-batch samples from new manufacturing site to CIL for analysis. The applicant is also required to submit last three (03) Years details of quantity imported from old source. It was further observed that the detailed guidelines shall be prepared on the above issues by the Sectt. of CIB&RC and put-up to RC in its next meeting specifying the compulsory submission of sample of 5 batch to CIL for analysis under verification of CC.

470.title: Consolidated Pendency Report relating applications for registration in CIB&RC
470.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and discussed the pendency of applications. It was noticed that the shortage of manpower is the main bottleneck in reducing the pendency to zero level. It was also explained that the huge data is submitted by the applicants under relevant categories, the same needs to scrutinized which needs time and other scientific and technical resources also needs to be studied which requires time. RC expressed it satisfaction over the quantum of work disposed by the Secretariat of CIB&RC at the same time directed the Secretariat to ask the applicants to submit the data as per guidelines, hence minimum deficiencies may be raised, to enhance the scrutiny process.

470.title: Pendency of application: Pending for more than 18 months that are deficient by one (1), two (2), and three (3) experts. It was observed that there are 155 files pending in the Secretariat of CIB&RC which are older than 18 months in various categories. Therefore, RC desired that all the experts should make more concise and dedicated efforts to clear all these 155 applications on priority. It was also decided that the tox files which consumes longer period in scrutiny such as TI/FI, TIM/FIM first time registration etc. may be redistributed among the existing tox experts to clear all these files on top most priority preferably on or before 08th April 2026. Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 RC also directed to get analyzed the PRV samples from CIL on priority for these applications, so pendency can be reduced to manageable level. It was further decided that a communication may be sent to CIL through PPA for doing the needful.

470.title: Follow up action of minutes of the Senior Officers meeting held on 09.03.2026 under the chairmanship of Secretary, DA&FW. Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 For bio-pesticide, revised guidelines to be finalized by first week of April, 2026. The time period and procedure for registration of pesticides licensing process should be rationalized & reformed for ease of doing business. Registration Committee (RC) has already simplified the guidelines for bio-pesticides. Provisional registration is granted under Section 9(3B) of the Insecticides Act, 1968 with permission for commercialization for two years, extendable for generating required data for regular registration under Section 9(3). Further, where a bio- pesticide strain is already registered in the country, no fresh data is required from new applicants, except confirmation of molecular identity from ICAR-NBAIM, Maunath Bhanjan (UP), and quality testing from the Central Insecticide Laboratory (CIL). The matter was deliberated during the 470th RC Meeting held on 23.03.2026. RC has observed that a significant bottleneck exists at the ICAR- NBAIM, Mau, specifically concerning the mandatory 1600s RNA molecular identification and DNA sequencing required for biopesticides (microbial). To address this and rationalize the registration procedure, the RC has proposed exploring additional institutes, such as ICAR-NBAIR in Bengaluru, which possess the necessary facilities for such identifications. By enabling the submission of samples to two institutes instead of one, the RC aims to significantly reduce the current pendency and streamline the registration process. A communication may be sent to the ICAR- NBAIR, Bengaluru to know their capabilities in the matter. Further, Sectt. Of CIB&RC has already issued strict instructions to all technical experts to complete the scrutiny of all files that have been pending for more than 18 months. These files are currently being scrutinized at an accelerated pace by all experts to ensure that the backlog is cleared within the stipulated time period.
470.product: pesticides licensing process should be rationalized & reformed for ease of doing business

469.title: Representation of Hindustan Pesticides Manufacturer Association (HPMA) for request to impose ban on import of agro-chemicals that Indian Industry is capable of producing- to support “Make in India” boost domestic manufacturing and reduce trade dependence. The agenda was deliberated in details on all aspects of the representation. During the elaborated discussion it was submitted by the Experts that the 9(3) original registrations are granted for the registration of an insecticide, after such enquiry as it deems fit and after satisfying itself that the insecticide to which the application relates conforms to the claims made by the importer or by the manufacturer, as the case may be, as regards the efficacy of the insecticide and its safety to human beings and animals. It was further noted that the IA, 1968 states that the 9(4) registrations can be granted on the basis of 9(3). The provision reads as under: Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 “Notwithstanding anything contained in the section where an insecticide has been registered on the application of any person, any other person desiring to import or manufacture the insecticide or engaged in the business of import or manufacture thereof, shall, on application and on payment of prescribed fee be allotted a registration number and granted a certificate of registration in respect thereof on the same conditions on which the insecticide was originally- registered.” The above provision infers that all the Registration of Product/Molecule has to be given a unique registration number and separate Registration Certificate has to be generated for each Molecule or Product to each applicant which shall be a mirror image of original registrant U/s 9(3) in terms of Chemical Composition etc. It was also informed that as per available information on the website more than 660 source of import are registered in India by the RC for Import of different molecules/products to be used in the country and very few applicants has submitted the complete details of source of import including the manufacturing address of the overseas country. After detailed evaluation of information and provisions the
469.decision: RC decided as under: 1. The Manufacturing address as well as office address of all the registered import sources of all the registered product/molecules registered for use in the country should be obtained from the stake holders with Geo Tagging details in the form of documentary evidence such as manufacturing license etc issued by the regulatory authorities of Source country/overseas country. The documents should be Government approved only. 2. The new applicants shall mandatorily submit the above required information with their applications. 3. The above said requirement shall also be treated as a part and parcel of the relevant applicable guidelines and shall also be included into the requirement in the guidelines. 4. 9(4) TI endorsement of additional Source shall not be allowed, if the Chemical Composition of already granted CR is different from the source sought to be endorsed. In such cases applicant has to obtained fresh CR as per guidelines U/s 9(4) TI category to enhance the transparency in case of quality control and collation of data. 5. 9(4) TI endorsement cases of extension of validity, Change of address, Purity of the product etc of such source shall not be permitted whose CC is different from 9(3) registrant and/or does not match with the 9(3) original registrant. (One Chemical Composition One CR is the principal rationale). The RC further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a public notice for appropriate compliance by all Stakeholders, copies of the same also be communicated to all Pesticides Associations for creating awareness to their member companies.

The Registration Committee (RC) further deliberated the agenda and observed that the formulation falls under Category 1: Serious damage to rabbit eyes (irreversible effects on the eye), and that as per the decision taken in the 398th RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 3.5), end- use products intended for use by farmers or other users which are classified as severely eye irritants shall not be registered for use in the country.

469.title: Consideration of an application of M/s Agro Life Science Corporation, for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Thiodicarb 50% + Imidacloprid 5% WDG u/s 9(3) FIM. The Registration Committee (RC) deliberated the agenda item and noted that the formulation falls under GHS Category-2 (>5–50 mg/kg b.wt.) with an LD₅₀ cut-off value of 50 mg/kg body weight, thereby falling under the red-coloured toxicity triangle. The Committee further noted the recommendations of the Dr. C.D. Mayee Committee that pesticides belonging to the extremely toxic (Red Triangle) category shall not be registered unless absolutely necessary and adequately justified. It was also observed that the formulation appears to be more toxic than the individual technical grade active ingredients and may attract the provisions of the RC decision taken in the 437th RC meeting regarding additional toxicity data where a formulation is more toxic than its technical. After deliberation, the
469.decision: RC decided that the applicant/stakeholder may be invited to make a detailed presentation addressing the necessity and justification for registration, toxicity concerns, and submission of additional toxicity data in compliance with the relevant RC decisions.

469.title: Follow up action on agenda item no. 10.71 of 468th RC meeting w.r.t. the order dated 05.01.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) in contempt petition (MD) No. 2710/2025 in WP (MD) No. 7813 of 2024 and presently the final order dated 09.01.2026. RC in terms of the observations made by the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) in its order dated 05.01.2026 had withdrawn its final decision taken in its 467th meeting at agenda item no. 2.2.
469.decision: RC perused the final judgement dated 09.01.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court and noted the same for compliance. Whereas Hon’ble High Court had directed the RC to take a fresh decision in the matter within a period of 4 weeks. RC shall accordingly draw the proceedings afresh in terms of the Hon’ble Appellate Authority order dated 21.03.2022 and the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) order dated 27.03.2024. Factual Background: Initially M/s Shobika was granted a provisional registration u/s 9(3b) of the Insecticides Act, 1968 at a concentration of 0.55% in the year 2015. Subsequent extensions were also granted for the same and the applicant had commercially used the product for several years. The applicant had applied for 9(3) registration for indigenous manufacture of Alphacypermethrin 0.58% in the year 2020. After due scrutiny of the application and after satisfying itself the RC approved the said application for a concentration of 0.55% in its 435th Meeting. Being dissatisfied with the 0.55% approval, the applicant approached the Hon’ble Appellate Authority by filing an appeal u/s 10 of the Insecticides Act, 1968. The following reasoning was given by the RC to grant registration at 0.55% instead of 0.58% in its impugned decision: 1. Appellant had previously applied for registration u/s 9(3B) of the Act for its LLIN containing 0.55% alphacypermethrin w/w as the active ingredient, which was granted along with commercialization. 2. There is no adverse report from the National Vector Borne Disease Control programme (NVBDCP) qua the LLINs with 0.55% active ingredient. 3. RC cannot consider registration for two products which have the same purpose but have different concentrations of the active ingredient. 4. RC follows the BIS specification wherein formulation compounds are given +10% and -5% of leverage which are under 9% of the active ingredients, where the Appellant had quoted + 25% of leverage, which may affect the quality of LLIN, which cannot be Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 permitted by the RC because, if permitted the appellant then “may have the right to manufacture LLINs at + 25% of the claimed items which have not been tested in Indian circumstances during generating the data to reveal their bio-effectiveness. The Hon’ble Appellate Authority after hearing M/s Shobika and the RC, had made certain observations and had set aside the decision of the RC taken on its 435th meeting at agenda item no. 11.2 wherein the RC had granted the registration on a concentration of 0.55%. Further, RC was directed to consider the application as per Form-I and technical information available on records. In terms of the above order although RC dealt the matter in its various meetings which are the part of record. In the mean while the applicant approached the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) by filing a writ petition no. 7813 of 2024 seeking directions to decide their captioned application of 0.58% in terms of the Appellate Authority Order. The Hon’ble High Court was pleased to pass an order dated 27.03.2024 directing the RC to consider and decide the application of the applicant for 0.58% in terms of the Appellate Authority Order. RC in its wisdom and in view of the fact that the substance sought to be registered is to be used in public health programmes and therefore, RC in order to scientifically deal with the matter had obtained comments from other related authorities including ICMR. Since, the RC was continuously deliberating the matter in its various meeting and hence could not take a final decision within the directed time lines. M/s Shobika had preferred a Contempt Petition before the Hon’ble High Court of Madras alleging willful non compliance of the Appellate Authority order dated 21.03.2022 and the Hon’ble High Court order dated 27.03.2024. During the pendency of the contempt petition the RC had taken a final decision in its 467th meeting at agenda item no. 2.2 whereby the RC has rejected the application of the applicant as the same does not qualify at 0.58% for the reasons mentioned in its final decision. The decision was in harmony of the Expert Committee Report from ICMR also. The Hon’ble High Court after adjudicating the matter had inter-alia found that the RC has committed a contempt by traveling outside the scope of the Appellate Authority Order and the order dated 27.03.2024 passed by the Hon’ble High Court. Now after going through the final order dated 09.01.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court and in terms of the observations made by the Appellate Authority in its order dated 21.03.2022 RC observes that although the RC had contested the matter on the grounds mentioned herein below:- 1. No new data was submitted along with Appellant application for registration under section 9(3) of the Act for LLIN containing 0.58% Alphacypermethrin w/w as the active ingredient. 2. The Appellant has not submitted toxicology data on “irritation to mucus membrane (rabbit)” for LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content of 0.58% w/w but has instead submitted the same for LLIN having alphacypermethrin content of 0.57% w/w. 3. Appellant has only generated Phase-III study data on LLIN containing Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w and Phase-1/Phase-II trial/evaluation were not be submitted for Appellant’s LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w. 4. The Appellant had earlier been given provisional registration u/s 9(3B) of the Act for the concentration of 0.55% w/w along with extensions during data generation which the registrant commercially used for about five years and during this period the petitioner had generated only Phase III study data on 0.58% w/w. Scientifically, to rely upon the phase-III study data on 0.58% w/w the petitioner ought to and should have also carried out the data generation for Phase-I and Phase-II at the concentration of 0.58% w/w. 5. That Phase-I and Phase-II studies were carried out at the concentration of 0.55% of alphacypermethrin and accordingly, the provisional certificate u/s 9(3B) with commercialization was granted. However, while applying for grant of registration u/s 9(3) Appellant claimed concentration of Alphacypermethrin at 0.58% which was claimed to be actually used only during Phase-III trial. M/s Shobika had also made the submission before the Appellate Authority as set out herein under :- a. The RC’s opposition to the grant of registration on the ground that the Appellant has not submitted toxicology data on “irritation to mucus membrane (Rabbit)” for LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content 0.58% w/w but has instead submitted the same for LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content of 0.57% w/w, is wholly misconceived and is contrary to its own agenda on toxicity produced by it. To this effect the appellant has relied on the following submission: i. Alphacypermethrin content of 0.57% w/w is well within the tolerance limit of ±25% that is appellant to this product. ii. Even the RC’s expert, in the above agenda on Toxicity did not point out hence, this is not a deficiency. On the contrary it was noted that the product was non irritant and the toxicity expert concluded after examining all toxicity data as under: “Appellant has submitted the data and information on the LLIN as per the laid down conventions guidelines, the case can be presented before the RC with complete fact for deliberation and appropriate decision”; b. Appellant further contends that he has already submitted three years, three locations bio-efficacy trial that were duly conduced in accordance with the protocol of Indian Council for Medical Research (ICMR). c. Further, RC is aware that as per ICMR protocol, Phase-I trial is not required in case the product has been approved by the WHO. RC is also aware that the Appellants product has already been approved by the WHO. d. Appellant has already conduct Phase-II trail prior to Phase -III trial for the product DuraNet with targeted dose containing 0.58% of Alphacypermethrin and the same was submitted during application made u/s 9(3B) of Insecticide Act, 1968. The National Institute of Malaria Research (NIMR), which has been established under the Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 aegis of the ICMR, has conducted the above mentioned Phase-II trail/evaluation for the product DuraNet (which was then owned by Clark Mosquito Control and has subsequently been purchased by the appellant) which target dose containing 0.58% w/w of alphacypermethrin ± 25%. Additionally, Vector Control Research Centre, Pondicherry (VCRC) has also conducted Phase-II trials/evaluation for the Appellant’s LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content of 0.58% w/w. e. Furthermore, RC never raised any query or demand for either Phase-I of Phase-II trials, nor did it raised any deficiency on the ground that Phase-I and Phase-II trials were not submitted for Appellant’s LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w. All this goes to shows that the RC’s suggestion at this stage that Appellant ought to have produced Phase-I and Phase-III trial, is misguided. The observations of the Hon’ble Appellate Authority have been recorded in para 8 of the order dated 21.03.2022and are as under: - It is a given fact that the Appellant product is based on the concentration which has applied for grant of registration u/s 9(3) and the RC ought to have considered the bio- efficacy and toxicity data related to this concentration, which was not done. This only goes to show that the RC’s decision in its 435th meeting vide agenda item no. 11.2 was indeed predetermined and not based on existing protocols and scientific justification. While taking the impugned decision in its 435th meeting for allowing registration of Alphacypermethrin 0.55%, The RC has not expressed any dissatisfaction with the data generated and submitted by the applicant using LLIN containing 0.58% Alphacypermethrin. In fact, that in the past RC has registered the different products for LLIN with Alphacypermethrin as active ingredient as different concentrations. Therefore, I agree that the only aspect the RC should have considered was safety and efficacy of the product at the concentration at which the present application u/s 9(3) of the Act has been made. The appellants submission on meeting all the protocols for generation of Phase-I, II and III trial data is based on clear scientific justification and existing protocols. Further as it revealed from the contents of impugned decision that RC never raised any query or demand asking for either Phase-I or Phase-II trails evaluations nor did it raised any deficiency on the ground that Phase-I and Phase-II trial evaluati9on were not submitted for the Appellant LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w. Therefore, RC’s observation in its written submission that the appellant ought to have produce Phase-I and Phase-II trail evaluation is an after thought. Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 It is fact that the LLINs are used worldwide and there is not scientific material relied upon by RC to suggest that mosquitoes has developed resistance to LLINs with Alphacypermethrin at 0.58% concentration. In fact own close perusal of the large scale bioefficacy trials conducted by National Central for Diseases Control (NCDC) on appellants product it is clear that the results are to the contrary. This appellate Authority gave CIB&RC ample scope to produce relevant scientific evidence on this aspects which CIB&RC could not be produce. Based on the contentions raised by the applicant and the CIB&RC; the Appellate Authority had recorded the above observations and accordingly the decision of the RC taken in its 435th meeting at agenda item no. 11.2 was set-aside and the directions were given to the RC to consider the grant of registration of the captioned application on 0.58% based on technical information available on record within a period of one month. Analysis: RC also observes that the submissions and contentions made by the RC before the Hon’ble Appellate Authority were not accepted and accordingly the decision of the 435th meeting was set-aside. RC also observes that the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) vide its order dated 05.01.2026 had clearly observed that the RC although had dealt the matter in its various meetings and had taken a final decision in 467th meeting traveling outside of the scope of the directions given by the Appellate Authority and has attempted to re-open the issues which were already adjudicated by the Appellate Authority. The Hon’ble High Court, in view of the fact that the decision of the RC taken in its 467th meeting stands withdrawn, has further been pleased to grant four weeks to pass a fresh order in terms of the directions given by the Appellate Authority and the Hon’ble High Court vide its order dated 27.03.2024. The RC perused the technical records pertaining to the matter and without entering into any further examination or analysis and in terms of the observations made by the Appellate Authority, notes that the tolerance limit of ± 25% although not applicable to the present matter but since the same is viewed by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority, the subject application of the applicant for 0.58% is again considered. RC also noted that since the matter has been adjudicated by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority and the Hon’ble High Court therefore, no further re-examination of the matter is needed. Accordingly, RC decided to grant the approval for LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin 0.58% w/w for indigenous manufacture to M/s Shobika. Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 RC makes it clear that this decision has been taken in the peculiar set of circumstances as enumerated above and shall not be construed as the precedent for any future purposes in any reference or case.

469.title: To explore provision for auto approval of preliminary scrutiny and cancellation or closure of applications for non-submission of requisite information within the stipulated time frame.
469.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in detail and decided as under: 1. As per the existing procedure, all the applications are passed through the preliminary scrutiny within a time limit of 5 days as on date. In this regard, the RC decided that the time limit of preliminary scrutiny may be extended to 7 days. Further, RC directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to ask the CGG to enhance the time limit upto 7 days in place of 5 days for preliminary scrutiny. 2. It shall be the responsibility of the concerned expert, if the file is not verified within 7 days or non-submission of data by the applicant as per applicable guidelines, excluding the genuine request for waiving off data. 3. It shall also be ensured that no file is accepted with lack of data whatsoever it may be, such as under generation of data for Shelf-Life OR bio-efficacy or any other data. 4. If, the file has been considered by the Experts during preliminary scrutiny, No deficiency shall be raised for lack of data and concerned Expert shall be solely responsible for this lapse. 5. The CGG may be asked to enable a provision for automated reminders/alerts to be generated through the CROP Portal on the 5th, 6th and 7thday to the concerned expert to ensure timely completion of preliminary scrutiny. It was also approved that the auto- approved files should also be flagged in the Secretary (CIB&RC) account for information and cognizance. 6. No file shall be moved to Park category, henceforth, if applicant is not submitting the deficiency reply in consonance of time line approved by RC in its 400th RC meeting vide agenda item No. 3.3. Such files will be closed automatically in CROP Portal and CGG has to make a provision for automatic closure of such applications. 7. All the applications under Parked category will be considered closed due to non- submission of response by the applicant as per 400th RC meeting decision of time line. The details of such files which stands approved as closed are attached as Annexure- 10.25.1. 8. Further, the RC directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a public Notice and ask the applicant to submit a requisition with relevant details to the RC within 30 days for revival of their application, if any. 9. If, any file is approved for opening or revival by the RC, after due consideration, in such scenario the applicant has to apply afresh and new file no. has to be generated by Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 the CROP. The scrutiny comments of the concerned Expert of such old closed/revived file may be taken into account. 10. It was also decided that the existing CROP Portal dashboard should have a feature for monitoring expert-wise performance for a desired period. Accordingly, the CGG team is directed to develop and incorporate suitable features in the Portal to enable monitoring and tracking of the performance of each expert. Such monitoring facility should be enabled in login of Department's Admin account. The RC also emphasized that there should be a section in the portal for tracking of file with complete history in chronological order.

Before consideration of the proposal of M/s FMC India Pvt. Ltd., for grant of registration for import of Tetflupyrolimet technical 91% w/w min. u/s section 9(3). The Registration Committee (RC) deliberated the agenda of M/s FMC India Pvt. Ltd. for registration of Tetflupyrolimet Technical (91% w/w minimum) under Section 9(3).
469.decision: The Committee noted concerns regarding the purity issue, as the applicant has sought registration of Tetflupyrolimet at 97% purity in the country of origin (USA), and the entire dossier has been generated using technical material with purity in the range of 99.1% to 96.06%. It indicates that the dossier has been prepared for a 97% product. BIS does not support such a purity gap (97% vs 91%), and even the EPA has reservations for this purity gap. The proposed 91% technical material represents a lower purity grade compared to the 97% product and may contain a higher proportion of impurities, which may require further refinement to meet higher purity specifications. (ii) implications of the DHODH mode of Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 action, on potential human and possible cross-resistance with medically relevant drugs specially antifungal drugs; India is a tropical country where fungal infections are prevalent, especially among agricultural workers due to prevailing conditions in the agricultural fields. (iii) immunotoxicity studies in view of the mechanism of action; and, as DHODH inhibition is linked to immune regulation (iv) PFAS-related concerns, including environmental persistence, degradation (such as TFA and other ultra-short-chain PFAS), and long-term toxicity aspects. After deliberation, the RC decided that the applicant/stakeholder be invited to make a detailed presentation addressing the above issues with supporting scientific data. The matter shall be considered thereafter.

468.title: Presentation by M/s Mahamaya Lifesciences Ltd., for grant of registration for technical import of Flonicamid technical 96% w/w min. u/s 9(3) TI (new source). The applicant made a presentation before the RC and submitted that the captioned application was submitted for the above product in terms of the extant guidelines of TI new source. The application was scrutinized by the RC by all the disciplines and each and every deficiency raised was duly responded to the satisfaction of the RC. The rejection of the above application by the RC in its 463rd meeting at agenda item no. 10.11 was on the ground that the technical of the product is not registered and hence the application is not maintainable. Challenging this decision before the Hon’ble Appellate Authority the Hon’ble Authority was pleased to set-aside the decision impugned in the matter and had made certain observation that the RC had already granted several registrations under TI new source in similar cases where the technical was not registered. Further, the Appellate Authority also observed that there is no explicit mention in the guidelines of TI new source presaging that the technical should be mandatorily registered before consideration of the application under TI new source. The applicant has thus requested to grant the registration for the above product under TI new source. RC was of the view that the applicant should submit the required information w.r.t. the detailed chemical composition of the source registered in the country of origin etc. and decided to grant the registration to the captioned product subject to the submission of requisite information. Secretariat of CIB&RC was instructed to verify the same before the issuance of certificate of registration.

468.title: Consideration of proforma/template for scrutiny of application under various categories of the Insecticides Act, 1968 for speeding-up of scrutiny process.
468.decision: The RC perused the agenda and deliberated the same in details and appreciated the vision and subsequent efforts put by the Sectt. of CIB&RC for devising the templates, spelling out the technical information extracted from the data in addition to the data submitted by the applicant as per the applicable guidelines to be furnished by the applicants w.r.t Chemistry, Toxicology, Bioassay and Packaging in order to facilitate the Sectt. of CIB&RC for speedy examination of applications under various categories of registration within the stipulated time as provided under the statute. The draft templates are annexed as Annexure-3.2.1. RC also directed that the approved draft templates developed by the Sectt. of CIB&RC shall be kept on public domain for inviting suggestions of the stakeholders within a period of 30 days from the date of hosting of the minutes. The Sectt. of CIB&RC is also directed to issue a public notice to this effect. The comments/inputs/suggestion so received shall be analyzed and the same may be placed before the RC for appropriate decision and implementation.

468.title: Non verification of registration certificate of M/s Meghmani Industries Ltd. Ahmedabad
468.decision: RC perused the agenda and expressed its serious concern on the issue of possessing of forged/fake certificate of registration for Sulphur 80% WDG purported to be issued vide Registration No. CIR-69,758/2005(254)-Sulphur (WDG-1125) from F.No.1,372-F 9(4)/2005 by M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad. The issue came to light when the company moved an application for the attestation of this certificate of registration and on being inquired about the genuineness of the same from available records at Sectt. of CIB&RC it was revealed that the above file no. doesn’t pertain to any such application for the grant of registration submitted by the M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad. Further the CR records that the above registration was approved by the RC in its 254th meeting on the contrary no such approval was found in the entire MOM of 254th meeting. Prima-facie RC is of the view that M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad is utilizing the above-mentioned CR which apparently appears to be fake and forged and, in any event, couldn’t be presumed as genuine. Such type of illegal activities is to be checked at the threshold with exemplary punishments to the wrong doers. RC still is inclined to grant an opportunity to show cause M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad before taking any further view in the matter. RC directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC to call M/s. Meghmani Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad to submit their point of view on the above aspect in the next RC.
