468.title: Submission of fake document/test report by M/s Sunshine Fine Chemsol (I) Pvt. Ltd.
468.decision: RC perused the agenda and took a serious note of the illegal activity of submission of fake and fabricated documents submitted by M/s Sunshine Fine Chemsol (I) Pvt. Ltd. for obtaining the registration. RC also observes that such an act by the company clearly tantamount to play fraud upon the RC, a statutory body constituted under the Insecticides Act, 1968. Such action also amounts to compromise with the safety and efficacy of the insecticide sought to be registered. Submission of forged reports without actual analysis/tests clearly amounts to defraud the authority which is a grave offence clearly covered within the definition of cheating, forgery and playing fraud upon the regulatory authority which may attract serious penal consequences including black listing of the company for future registration and cancellation of the earlier registrations granted along with other legal actions in accordance with law. RC also observed that a Show Cause Notice dated 03.12.2025 had already been issued to the company to provide their clarification/stand in this regard on which the company had sought time to submit the same. RC observes that although the issue is extremely serious but RC feels expedient that a final opportunity may be given to the company to Show Cause as to why legal proceedings may not be initiated against them. RC decided that M/s Sunshine Fine Chemsol (I) Pvt. Ltd. is granted fifteen days time from the communication of this decision to submit their explanation with supporting documents in this regard failing which appropriate legal proceedings/action both in civil and criminal side shall be initiated against the company.

468.title: Representation with a request for action against Chinese company engaged in malpractices leading to illegal import. Minutes of 468th RC meeting held on 12.01.2026
468.decision: RC perused the email communication dated 29.05.2025 received from Mr. Amit Sahni advocate addressed to Chairman RC with a request to take action against Chinese companies engaged frequently in malpractices leading to illegal imports and obtaining product registration in India which is an issue of public interest. It is also inter-alia pointed out that several Chinese companies post registration alter their manufacturing process, shift or close down their approved facilities and continue exporting the product to India from different unapproved sources often without updating the regulatory bodies. This not only undermines the integrity of the regulatory framework but also poses serious risks to Indian manufacturers, consumers and farmers, as the imported products are not re- evaluated for safety or efficacy. The advocate had thus requested that being a serious matter appropriate steps be taken against the violators to curb such practices that compromise regulatory integrity endanger public safety. RC is of the firm view that the concerns raised are serious in nature and needs examination at the level of Sectt. of CIB&RC. RC directs the concerned technical experts dealing import registration and further the issues related to the source of import etc. to examine the entire gamut of issue raised and ensure to place a factual report before the next RC meeting for taking an appropriate view in the matter.

RC decided to comply with the order dated 19.11.2025. RC also observes that the Central Government (DA&FW), after legal opinion and scrutiny, had published draft rules for the requirement of the import permit for all insecticides proposed to be used for non- insecticidal/industrial purposes. RC recalls that similar issues were also dealt in its 395th, 397th, 400th and 401st meetings. RC also notes that the import permits are being granted as per simplified guidelines and as an exemption for registration when the use of such substances is non insecticidal. RC is also of the view that the DGFT Ministry of Commerce can issue a notification for its import and export policies by the virtue of Section 5 of the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992. RC decided that DA&FW may be requested to issue a suitable communication to the DGFT to issue a notification for the requirement of the import permit for all substances which are proposed to be imported for non-insecticidal use. 468.title: Illegal trade of Methyl Bromide causing serious damage to Ozone layer and tax evasion to the Government of India and State Government.
468.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that an email communication dated 14.11.2025 and 03.12.2025 addressed to various Authorities including Sr. officers of DA&FW, PPA and Secretary, CIB&RC has been received from Green Envir pointing out the illegal trade and other unethical activities carried out by M/s Intech Organics Ltd.,/Intech Pharma ltd., who is manufacturing methyl bromide and vinyl bromide along with other products in Rajasthan and Goa inter-alia it has also been pointed out that the firm has exported a consignment of methyl bromide to Libya in the name of vinyl bromide which was caught and thus it is an illegal trade. It is also alleged that the firm is selling methyl bromide in the name of vinyl bromide and exporting it to the countries like Libya although the same is banned in Libya. It is also pointed out that they do not have any facilities/infrastructure Minutes of 468th RC meeting held on 12.01.2026 to produce vinyl bromide in any of their plants. Some more instances of unethical activities carried out by the firm M/s Intech are also pointed out. RC observes that the issues raised in the communication are extremely sensitive as the product methyl bromide has a direct impact on the environment and is capable of causing damage to the Ozone layer. RC took a serious view on such unethical activities carried out by M/s Intech and the same appears to be a breach/violation of the laws of the land. RC feels it expedient that before taking any coercive steps against M/s Intech an opportunity to Show Cause may be granted to them to seek their clarification/justification in this regard. RC directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a Show Cause Notice to the firm granting them 15 days time to submit a response thereto.
